 Shares of Tata Consumer Products gained up to 4.5% to their day's high of Rs 979 on the BSE on Tuesday after the FMCG major released its results for the July-September quarter of FY27, reporting a 16% year-on-year growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 469 crore despite higher costs and weak tea demand.on-year growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 469 crore despite higher costs and weak tea demand.
 Tata Consumer Products said its revenue from operations stood at Rs 5,661 crore for the second quarter of FY27, up 14% from Rs 4,966 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. The firm’s consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) meanwhile increased 18% to Rs 794 crore during the quarter.
“We delivered our second consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth in FY27, backed by strong underlying volume growth in India business. This volume-led performance, together with disciplined execution, drove 18% EBITDA growth,” said Sunil D’Souza, managing director and chief executive officer of Tata Consumer Products.
 Also read | Tata Consumer Q2 Results: Net profit rises 16% YoY to Rs 470 crore, revenue up 14% 
 Jefferies on Tata Consumer Products share price
 Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Tata Consumer Products shares but reduced its target price to Rs 1,250 apiece from Rs 1,450. The latest target price implies around 33.5% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price.
 Live Events
The international brokerage noted that Tata Consumer Products remains a key beneficiary of the rapid adoption of quick commerce, especially in the growth portfolio, which contributed around 38% of the India business in the second quarter, with this share set to reach around 50% in three years.
Overall, the FMCG major’s Q2 performance was ahead of estimates despite inflationary pressures in tea and salt segments, but product price hikes should help in future, according to Jefferies. International business saw a revenue decline but saw margin expansion.
 Nuvama on Tata Consumer Products share price
 Nuvama Institutional Equities maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the shares of Tata Consumer Products, but reduced its target price to Rs 1,275 apiece, implying over 36% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price. The brokerage noted that the company’s Q2 earnings print was in line with estimates.
The brokerages reduced the target price to factor in the EPS estimate cuts and inflationary pressures in the economy.
 Elara Capital on Tata Consumer Products share price
 Elara Capital reiterated its ‘Accumulate’ call on shares of Tata Consumer Products but reduced its target price to Rs 1,080 apiece from Rs 1,290. The latest target price implies more than 15% upside potential.
The brokerage noted that the company’s 14% revenue growth was in line with estimates, according to ET Now. It added that the valuation contribution from Tata Starbucks JV was revised to Rs 40 per share from Rs 54.
 Systematix on Tata Consumer Products share price
 Systematix Institutional Equities upgraded its rating on the shares of Tata Consumer Products to ‘Buy’ but reduced its target price to Rs 1,185 apiece from Rs 1,245 apiece. It noted that the company delivered the tenth straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth.
Tata Consumer Products is consistently generating strong double-digit topline growth across most segments (excluding India tea) for the past five-six quarters now, led by sturdy volume growth, the domestic brokerage noted. In addition, the portfolio is pivoting towards higher-growth businesses, like Sampann, Soulfull, RTD, which are also now starting to assert themselves on margins, it added.
While this transformation could likely be gradual, it reduces dependence on the seasonal tea business, Systematix said. “We also like the near- to medium-term margin construct with product mix enrichment accruing from premium variants of pulses, dry fruits, breakfast cereals, snacks (poha, makhana), RTD beverages and cold-pressed oils. The recent sharp stock price correction (-19% over the past 6 months) provides downside comfort,” it added.
 Also read | Tata consumer Q2 net profit up despite higher costs, weak tea demand 
 Tata Consumer Products share price
Tata Consumer Products shares have fallen more than 3% in the past one week and around 5% in a month, with the stock being down more than 20% in 2026 so far.
In the longer term, shares of the FMCG major have delivered positive returns of a little over 6% in three years and 15% in five years. The company has a market capitalisation of more than Rs 92,685 crore.

 Ather Energy shares jumped another 5% on Tuesday, extending their two-day rally to 20% after the company’s Q2 results impressed brokerages and prompted several target price hikes.
 Ather Energy shares rose to Rs 1,660 apiece on the NSE on Tuesday morning. The electric scooter maker reported its first quarterly net profit of Rs 1.26 crore in the September quarter of FY27, marking a sharp turnaround from a net loss of Rs 154 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue grew nearly 63% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 1,464 crore, supporting the turnaround.
The company’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) turned positive at Rs 11.3 crore, against an EBITDA loss of Rs 133 crore a year earlier. The EBITDA margin stood at 0.77%. “We are not out of the woods. There is a lot of work for us to deliver on. The focus is on the top line. Improving volume will itself take care of operating leverage, if all the capacity work we are putting in bears fruit over the next few months. In the near term it can go up and down, but it is definitely worth celebrating this milestone for the business,” Tarun Mehta, CEO, Ather Energy, said.
 Also read | Ather Energy swings to first quarterly profit as revenue rises 63% 
 Nomura on Ather Energy share price
Nomura increased its target price for the shares of Ather Energy to Rs 2,070 apiece from Rs 1,926 apiece, while maintaining its ‘Buy’ rating. The latest target price implies more than 31% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 1,575 apiece.
 Live Events
The international brokerage reaffirmed Ather Energy as its top pick in the two wheeler space. It noted that the company’s industry-leading tech pack, improving reach, and product portfolio makes it best-positioned to benefit from the EV inflection and resulting increase in EV salience of OEMs.
 Ather Energy share price
Ather Energy shares have jumped 13% in a week and 11% in a month. The stock has delivered multibagger returns of more than 124% in 2026 so far.
Overall, the shares of the company have jumped 126% in one year. The company currently has a market capitalisation of nearly Rs 65,790 crore.

docs.title: Britain issues costliest 5-year debt since 2008 before budget
docs.text:
Britain sold £4.5 billion ($6.0 billion) of 5-year debt on Tuesday, paying an average yield of 5.036%, the highest since 2008, and showing the bond market pressure on finance minister John Healey before his first annual budget on Wednesday.
 Investors bid for 3.51 times the volume on offer of the 4.625% March 2032 gilt, the UK Debt Management Office said, typical of the strong demand for British government bonds this year.

Bond yields have surged across advanced economies since the start of the US-Iran war, pushing up the cost of new government borrowing, as investors fear higher inflation and debt issuance due to the jump in energy prices.
Earlier this month, 20- and 30-year gilt yields hit their highest since 1998, while 5- and 10-year yields reached their highest since 2008.
Gilt dealers polled by Reuters last week expect only a modest increase in debt issuance this financial year after the budget, pencilling in a median £3.4 billion rise in gilt sales and a £5 billion increase in net sales of Treasury bills.

But they see a chunkier £27 billion rise in the country's gross financing requirement for 2027/28, compared with the last official forecast in March, to £334 billion. They also expect long-dated gilt issuance this year to fall to its lowest since 1990/91 as the DMO targets cheaper shorter-dated financing.
In March, before most of the rise in gilt yields, the UK Office for Budget Responsibility predicted Britain would spend 3.8% of national income servicing public debt by the end of the decade, nearly twice as much as in the 2010s.

docs.title: When will your Social Security payment arrive in November 2026? Two dates shift, and SSI gets paid early
docs.text:
Social Security payments for November will reach beneficiaries on different days, and the usual calendar has shifted a little this time. Two things cause this; November 1 falls on a Sunday, and Veterans Day comes on Wednesday, November 11.
 The Social Security Administration (SSA) pays nearly 72 million people. They include retired workers, people with disabilities, and the spouses and survivors of eligible workers. The date of payment depends on the type of benefit, when the person started claiming it and, for most people, their birth date.
 Here is the schedule: 
 October 30: SSI payment for November. Since November 1 is a Sunday, it comes early.
 November 3: For people who started getting benefits before May 1997, and for those who receive both Social Security and SSI.
 November 10: For people born between the 1st and 10th of any month. This is one day earlier than normal because of the Veterans Day holiday on November 11.
 November 18: For people born between the 11th and 20th.
 November 25: For people born between the 21st and 31st.
 What the 3.6 percent raise means
On October 14, the SSA announced a cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) of 3.6 percent for 2027. This is higher than the 2.8 percent raise given in 2026. About 76 million people who get Social Security or SSI will see their monthly amount go up from next year. This number is higher than the 72 million above because it also counts SSI recipients.
 Here is what the SSA expects: 
 Live Events
 Average retired worker: from $2,095 to $2,170 a month, a rise of $75.
 Couples where both spouses get retirement benefits: from $3,238 to $3,355 combined.
 Disabled workers: from $1,642 to $1,701.
 Maximum SSI for one person: from $994 to $1,029.
 Maximum SSI for a couple: from $1,491 to $1,544.
 The COLA is based on the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W), a measure of inflation prepared by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The SSA takes the average CPI-W of July, August and September and compares it with the same three months of the previous year. The difference in percentage becomes the next year’s COLA.
Before the COLA announcement, AARP surveyed Americans and asked about a possible 3.5 percent COLA. Among people aged 50 and above, 76 percent said it would not be enough to keep up with prices. Among those already getting Social Security, the figure was 80 percent.

docs.title: India to remain top of the Asian pie for Advent
docs.text:
Mumbai: India will be the largest market for Advent International in Asia as the Boston based private equity group has successfully raised $30 billion for a new global buyout fund and a newer mid-market fund , beating the slowdown that has plagued several top tier funds this year.
 Advent, majority owned by its partners, exceeded its target by raising close to $27 billion for its 11th flagship fund Advent International GPE XI, making it one of the world’s largest pools for buyout funds, it said in a statement on Tuesday.
 Also Read: Advent International joins India’s hospital gold rush with Rs 3,150 crore Yatharth bet 
Advent raised its last flagship fund in 2022 at $25 billion.
“I believe this should be a good vintage of investing in India,” said Shweta Jalan , Managing Partner. “There have been a few external headwinds for the economy, like oil price volatility and currency fluctuations, but on balance mid to long term, we genuinely believe this is a good place to invest.”
 Live Events
In the last 19 years, since it’s first investment, Advent has invested around $7.5 billion in the country, executing 23 investments in total across a range of sectors that includes banks, packaging, pharmaceuticals, tech services and lending.
Asia-Pacific now accounts for nearly a fifth of Advent’s active portfolio by company count and around 17% of the total 109 billion of assets it currently manages. Its footprint in the region is also expanding. Since 2024, it has opened three new beach heads in Australia, Japan and Hong Kong. Jalan said the fund made its debut investment in Japan, a market that has seen a revival in dealmaking after a long hiatus, earlier this year. It has made 2 transactions in Australia in as many years.
Jalan is confident that with the new dry powder, the fund will be able to double down on all 5 key sectors it focuses on – pharma and healthcare, financial services, consumer, technology services and AI and finally industrials.
Within industrials, sub-sectors like chemicals, auto components and AI infrastructure have emerged as dominant themes.
 Also Read: AI is rewriting the rules of investment for India's big-ticket players 
“We have seen and endured several business cycles across India over the last two decades. Our underlying belief remains that India will sustain healthy GDP growth and our track record will help ensure India remains the biggest contributor to our Asia portfolio. Long term, this is a defensible growth story,” added Jalan.
This calendar year has been among the firm’s most active years for realizations. Year to date the firm has realised approximately $13 billion across 27 businesses. Some of its headline grabbing exits, also the biggest across the PE industry, include the sale of TK Elevator, alongside Cinven, to Kone Oyi for $34 billion, including debt. The buyout firm also took gas engine manufacturer Innio Holding GmbH public in a US IPO, as the company joined a slew of industrial companies looking to tap the surge in data-center spending. Rather than relying heavily on sponsor-to-sponsor transactions or initial public offerings, a large portion of exits involved sales to corporate strategic buyers, or to other PE groups.
“The trust our investors have placed in us in one of the most demanding fundraising environments reflects the consistency of our track record and our discipline in returning capital,” said John Maldonado, Managing Partner, Advent. Maldonando is also the co-shair of the firm’s Executive Committee.
Over 50% of commitments for the Advent funds came from public pension funds and sovereign wealth funds, alongside family offices, insurance companies, endowments and foundations, institutional fund managers and high-net-worth individuals. Over 80% came from existing investors. This makes them an outlier when limited partners have become increasingly choosy to back PE groups with funding commitments. Private equity funds, in particular, have been under siege by investors to return capital and sell more companies, many of which were bought at lofty valuations, during the Covid buyout frenzy of 2000-2022.
This in turn, has led to funds being forced to reconsider their fundraising plans or lower expectations for new funds as well as returns. Overpaying for companies has led to a massive backlog in the private equity industry on the exit side. Funds put deals on hold as sellers and buyers couldn’t agree on prices, especially for the funds the firms bought during the Covid buyout frenzy.
The group has also deployed approximately $10 billion across 38 new and existing businesses. In India, it has deployed over $875 million (Rs 8,250 crore) across three transactions this year alone in Yatharth Hospitals, Iscon Balaji and Aditya Birla Housing Finance and launched a sale process to exit DFM Foods, a snack foods company it took private.
The firm, led by a group of managing partners including Maldonado and James Brocklebank, is known for its focus on buyouts. In India, however it has been flexible and have backed companies with growth equity as well as outright control transactions. For example, all its transactions in CY26 are for significant minority stakes.
The $3 billion Mid-Market Fund is Advent's first dedicated vehicle targeting smaller buyouts and growth investments with a focus on investing equity of $100 million to $350 million in companies with enterprise values of up to $1.25 billion primarily in North America and Europe.

docs.title: Adani-group owned ACC’s consolidated profit slumps 92% on year in September quarter
docs.text:
MUMBAI: Adani group-owned ACC ’s profit nosedived 92% year-on-year in the September quarter as sales volumes were lower, costs were higher and as the year-ago period had the benefit of a large tax write-back. It reported a profit of Rs 93 crore for Jul-Sep; this compares to Rs 1,119 crore in the year ago period, which had a tax writeback of Rs 671 crore.
 The cement producer reported its earnings during market hours on Tuesday, reacting to which its shares hit their 52-week low of Rs 1,115 on the BSE. The shares closed at Rs 1,147.50 on the BSE, down 1.6% from the previous close.
The company sold 9.7 million tonne of cement during the September quarter, down from 10 million tonne a year ago. This includes the impact of the Master Supply Agreement (MSA) with Ambuja Cements , where it supplied higher volumes to the parent entity. Consolidated revenue from operations also fell a little over 5% to Rs 5,689 crore from Rs 6,005 crore earlier.
“While the reported numbers are not strictly comparable due to the impact of MSA, the underlying business momentum remains encouraging, supported by our trade partners,” chief executive officer Vinod Bahety said.
Total expenses for the period rose over 2% on year to Rs 5,602 crore despite the fall in revenue.
 Live Events
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, meanwhile, more than halved to Rs 401 crore from Rs 846 crore a year ago. Operating margins, too, halved to 7.0% from 14.1% a year ago, while the EBITDA made on each tonne of cement fell to Rs 414 from Rs 849 a year ago.
“Industry demand remains supportive and is expected to strengthen post-monsoon, aided by housing, infrastructure and capital expenditure, while improving pricing momentum should moderate the impact of elevated fuel and energy costs,” Bahety said.
The company said that it expects demand in the medium-term to be supported by infrastructure investment, urbanisation, rural housing and industrial activity. Capital expenditure by the central government increased 18% on year to Rs 5.1 lakh crore during Apr–Aug this year, compared with Rs 4.3 lakh crore in the corresponding period last year, the company said.

India's 6.94% 2036 bond yield was down 1 basis point at 7.4732% as of 10:55 a.m. IST. Bond yields move inversely to prices.
 Bonds Corner

 Indian bonds tick up on calm oil before Fed verdict In early trade, Indian government bonds improved as oil prices found stability after last week's surge. Traders remained cautious ahead of a significant policy decision by the US Federal Reserve on Wednesday. India's bond yields decreased slightly, although overall demand for longer maturities has declined amid inflation concerns. The 1-year OIS rate eased marginally to 6.65%, but still implied odds of over 100 basis points of rate hikes over the next year.

docs.title: How to get maximum value when buying a budget-friendly used car
docs.text:
A tight budget doesn't mean settling for a bad car. It means being stricter about what gets checked. Most people who overspend on a used car don't overspend at the point of sale; they overspend across the six months that follow, on clutch kits, tyres, suspension bushes and a battery that was already halfway dead when they signed the papers. The buying process is where that money is either saved or quietly lost.
 Fix the real budget, not the sticker budget
A significant portion of the real cost sits outside the sticker price. Ownership transfer charges, a fresh insurance policy, a possible smart card RC fee, and the first round of consumables all add up before the car moves an inch.
Anyone shortlisting the cheapest used cars in India should ring-fence a meaningful buffer for these costs before even opening a listings page. 
Here's what actually happens: a buyer stretches to the very top of their budget chasing a slightly newer model, feels great about the deal, then delays a timing belt change or runs on tyres with a manufacture date from five years ago because the cash ran out. That saving disappears within a season. Sometimes faster.
Segment context matters more than most buyers realise. A comparable European hatchback at the same price can cost twice as much to keep running; sensors and suspension components that take weeks to source from the distributor will do that to you.
 Live Events
 The inspection that separates a good buy from a money pit
Spend more time under the car than inside it.
When viewing privately, a paint thickness gauge is the single most useful tool you can bring. The factory paint on most mass-market Indian cars reads in a fairly narrow band, and a panel showing wildly higher numbers has been repainted.
One repainted door is normal wear. Three adjacent panels plus a repainted pillar suggest structural repair, which is a completely different conversation.
Check the chassis number plate for tampering, rusting or fresh punch marks. Lift the boot carpet and look at the spare wheel well for ripples or non-factory welds. Rear-end impacts hide there frequently.
 Cold starts tell the truth
A car warmed up before you arrive is hiding something - tappet noise, a smoky first crank, a battery that won't hold charge under load. Insist on a genuinely cold engine, then just listen for the first ten seconds.
You'll hear more in that window than in twenty minutes of driving. Rattles settle in, smoke shows itself, and an iffy idle becomes obvious before the seller can distract you with features.
 Quick checklist worth running on every budget car
 Tyre DOT codes: anything over five years old needs replacing regardless of how much tread remains
 Clutch bite point should engage low, not near the top of the pedal travel where it's already halfway worn
 Steering play and knocking over speed breakers
 AC cooling after ten minutes of idling, not a thirty-second blast in the showroom
 Service history stamps or workshop invoices - regular oil changes, not just one tidy-up service done right before listing
 The odometer is easy to cross-check against pedal rubbers, the steering wheel and the driver's seat bolster. A car showing 40,000 km with a polished brake pedal and a collapsed seat cushion hasn't done 40,000 km. It's been rolled back, and that happens more often than buyers expect in this segment.
For complete peace of mind, look at listings for cars under 5 lakhs which have been pre-inspected thoroughly, including both mechanical and ownership history.
 Budget for the first ninety days
Assume the car arrives needing work. Not because sellers are dishonest - many aren't - but because most people selling a budget car weren't servicing it on a strict schedule in the first place.
Engine oil, oil filter, air filter, brake fluid and coolant should all be treated as due unless invoices prove otherwise. Batteries carry a manufacturing date sticker, and anything past three years is living on borrowed time, especially through a hot Indian summer.
Timing belts are an expensive surprise. Many older petrol engines specify replacement at a certain mileage interval, and a snapped belt on an interference engine doesn't just leave you stranded - it can write off the cylinder head entirely.
Ask for that invoice specifically. No invoice? Factor the replacement cost into your offer, or walk.
A properly serviced budget hatchback usually needs consumables and little else in the first year. One that's been neglected will ask for suspension, brakes and clutch in quick succession. That's the actual difference between a cheap car and an expensive one.

docs.title: Flexible workspace providers go bigger on solar
docs.text:
Managed office operators are no longer treating renewable power as a utility-side add-on. Across India, large flexible workspace providers are moving beyond rooftop panels and into captive solar farms, a shift that ties real estate strategy to long-term energy planning, tenant expectations and carbon targets. 
That change is being led by listed and scaled operators such as IndiQube, Table Space and WeWork India , each of which is building or expanding solar capacity to serve its portfolio of offices. The common thread is simple: in a market where enterprise occupiers increasingly ask for cleaner buildings, workspace providers are trying to control both the source and the cost of electricity. 
 From rooftops to utility-scale supply 
IndiQube has already crossed 30 megawatt of operational solar capacity and is aiming to add nearly 30 MW more in the current financial year. The company’s footprint includes solar farms in Karnataka and Maharashtra, more than 25 rooftop installations across the country, and another solar project in Tamil Nadu that is expected to widen that network further. 
 Rishi Das , co-founder and chief executive of IndiQube, said the company sees power transition and building efficiency as linked rather than separate exercises. He said the near-term goal is to move the portfolio to 100 per cent green power, with renewable capacity expanding in step with workplace growth. In his view, solar investment and green building upgrades reinforce one another by improving how a property performs while also changing the energy source behind that performance. 
 The company is now pushing the idea further, framing it as “managed green power” rather than only managed workspaces. Das said the initial effort began with meeting internal demand, but the broader opportunity is to help other enterprises shift in the same direction. 
 Why flexible workspace operators have an edge 
The business model itself gives these operators an advantage that conventional office landlords often lack. Managed workspace platforms can pool demand from multiple centres and multiple customers, which creates enough scale to justify larger renewable investments. That makes it easier to move from isolated rooftop systems to off-site solar farms that can serve a wider portfolio. 
 This matters because many office buildings are leased, limiting how much rooftop capacity a workspace operator can deploy on its own. Table Space president and co-chief executive Kunal Mehra said rooftop solar alone cannot meet the electricity needs of a large office campus when most centres sit in leased properties. He added that the company’s recent captive solar investment was designed to create additionality in the market through an equity stake in an off-site project, with power delivered through open access. Where roof area is available, Table Space supplements that with on-site solar and renewable energy certificates. 
 Table Space builds a broader clean power stack 
Table Space has invested in captive solar capacity of about 3.8 MWp across Karnataka and Maharashtra. In partnership with Clean Max and AMPYR Energy , the renewable projects are expected to deliver more than 5 million units of clean electricity each year and avoid roughly 3,500 tonnes of emissions annually, according to the company. 
As of March 31, Table Space’s portfolio covered 11.46 million sq ft across 176 facilities and 84 centres in nine cities. Mehra said many of the company’s enterprise clients now come with their own net-zero commitments, which is raising the bar for the workspaces they occupy. For those customers, clean power is becoming part of the lease decision rather than a side benefit. 
 Mehra said long-term renewable investments should also improve predictability in energy costs and are expected to double the share of renewable energy in the company’s energy mix. He added that the clean power plan supports Table Space’s net-zero commitment and its efforts to set science-based targets through the Science Based Targets initiative . 
 WeWork India looks to lock in power for the next quarter century 
WeWork India is taking a more direct ownership route with a planned 10 MWp DC ground-mounted solar plant in Karnataka. The project is expected to be commissioned in the current financial year and is part of the company’s goal of moving to 100 per cent renewable electricity by March 2028. 
The plant is projected to generate about 15 million to 16 million units of clean power annually. Once operational, it is expected to lift the renewable share in the company’s portfolio to about 50 per cent from nearly 40 per cent now. 
About 80 per cent of the output will be used for WeWork India’s own operations, including 10 centres in Bengaluru. The remaining 20 per cent will support future expansion. Managing director and chief executive Karan Virwani has said Bengaluru is the company’s largest market, making it the logical place to start a renewable investment of this scale. He has also argued that the move is as much about business discipline as sustainability, since owning generation capacity can reduce operational emissions while giving the company greater certainty over energy costs for 25 years. 
 What the shift means for India’s office market 
The move by managed workspace operators signals a wider change in how commercial real estate is approaching sustainability. Clean power is no longer confined to developer-led green certifications or tenant-led procurement. In the flexible workspace segment, operators themselves are becoming energy aggregators, investors and, increasingly, generators. 
That shift could matter beyond the sector. As more enterprises ask for lower-carbon workplaces, workspace providers that can bundle real estate with renewable electricity may gain an edge in occupier retention and new business wins. docs.title: IndiaMART bets on AI to sharpen its edge, but warns of uncertain returns
docs.text:
IndiaMART InterMESH Ltd outlined its growing use of artificial intelligence across business operations during its earnings call for the second quarter ended September 2026. The B2B e-commerce company said it is deploying AI across multiple functions while leveraging different AI models, as it looks to explore new opportunities and strengthen its competitive position.
 Read more: L&T flags inflation, geopolitical risks, leans on its capabilities to navigate global uncertainty 
“AI is being deployed across more than 20 functions, ranging from pre-sales and data preparation to sales meeting scheduling, service ticket resolution, catalogue design, category mapping, audits, user verification and category intelligence,” said Dinesh Agarwal , Chief Executive Officer of IndiaMART InterMESH Ltd, during the earnings call. 
“For over a year now, our voice AI agents have been serving around 80,000 to 1 lakh buyers every day. Buy leads and requests for quotations (RFQs) generated through these interactions are posted live on the IndiaMART platform,” Agarwal said.
Read more: IndiaMART doubles down on AI to curb fake listings, improve buyer interaction 
 Live Events
On the company’s choice of AI models, Agarwal said IndiaMART uses a range of solutions, including Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemma, Alibaba’s Qwen and Grok. He added that the company generally prefers to use existing models rather than develop them in-house, as AI development is not its core business.
“AI is helping us in many areas where we could not do certain things earlier. At the same time, it is putting similar tools in the hands of the public, allowing them to do many things on their own,” he said, adding that the net impact of AI on the business could remain volatile over the next two to four years.
Agarwal said IndiaMART’s data could become a key competitive advantage if used effectively with AI. “AI and your IndiaMART data, if used effectively, can actually become a very useful force in protecting your turf and growing your turf in the times to come,” he said.
He also said the company had begun gradually integrating BUSY, Livekeeping and IndiaMART at the backend.
“While AI is opening up several opportunities that we could not explore earlier, it is also putting similar tools in the hands of the public, allowing them to do many things on their own. The net benefit of AI over the next two to four years could remain volatile. However, our deeper understanding of the technology and its applications provides some downside protection. We understand AI, we are using it effectively, and we see several opportunities in this space,” said Agarwal.
The B2B e-commerce company reported a 9.8% year-on-year y-o-y rise in net profit to Rs 90.8 crore in the second quarter ended September 2026, compared with Rs 82.7 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Revenue from operations increased 9.7% YoY to Rs 429 crore from Rs 391 crore a year earlier.
Consolidated customer collections grew 9% YoY to Rs 443 crore during the quarter.

docs.title: Jonathan Bailey's £1.5 million home: Why the 'Wicked' star chose England's South Coast
docs.text:
Jonathan Bailey swapped London for life by the sea, buying a £1.5 million home on the Sussex coast last year. The Wicked star chose a four-bedroom villa near Brighton and Hove , close to family and the outdoor activities he enjoys. The move came as Bailey’s profile continued to rise, with roles in Bridgerton, Jurassic World Rebirth and the Wicked films bringing him wider attention. Although he was named People magazine’s Sexiest Man Alive in 2025, the title has since passed to a new star in 2026.
 Why did Jonathan Bailey choose Brighton and Hove
Bailey bought the property in an area on the border of Brighton and Hove that locals reportedly call “millionaires’ row”. The £1.5 million home has four bedrooms and sits in a sought after seaside enclave. One source described the location as a favourite among famous names. “It's A-list heaven where he is,” the source said. “It's one of the most amazing spots in the UK. It just shows what some cash from starring in blockbuster movies can buy.” The inputs are taken from The Daily Mail and Thr Argus. 
Bailey’s neighbours include comedian David Walliams, musician Fatboy Slim and former Heartbeat actor Nick Berry. Paul McCartney and Adele have also owned homes in the area in the past.
The move reflects Bailey’s wish to spend more time near his family. He grew up in Oxfordshire, in the village of Brightwell cum Sotwell and later moved away from London during the pandemic.
 Live Events

 What does Bailey love about life by the sea
Bailey told The New York Times that he moved to the Sussex coast between lockdowns to be closer to his family. “My mom’s side of the family was always by the sea, and I guess I’ve inherited that gene,” he said.
The actor has also spoken about his enjoyment of cold-water swimming and outdoor activities.
“I like outdoor activities that are bracing and stimulating: Being against, and leaning into, the elements has always been quite rewarding and meditative,” he said.

He added, “It gives your mind and body the same experience at the same time, which feels like a reset, if just for a few minutes.”
People magazine named him its Sexiest Man Alive, making him the first openly gay man to receive the title in 2025.
In 2026, the title went to actor Noah Wyle, known for The Pitt and ER. Bailey’s 2025 honour remains a milestone in his career, which has continued to grow alongside his move to the English coast.

docs.text:

Her comments came days after a group of creditors hired restructuring advisers PJT Partners and Akin Gump, according to media reports, fueling speculation about the airline's ability to manage its debt while struggling to return to profitability.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.
 The board has set the issue price at Rs 33 per share.
The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.

— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

 Paytm shares to focus after reporting a sharp Q2 profit rise.

Paytm shares are set to be in the spotlight on Tuesday after the fintech company reported a sharp rise in fiscal second quarter profit and an improvement in operating margins. Brokerages including Jefferies, Citi, Goldman Sachs and Bernstein maintained bullish ratings on the stock. Analysts cited strong growth in financial services, improving profitability and potential gains from the proposed UPI merchant discount rate (MDR).
Bernstein has the highest target price of Rs 2,200 on Paytm stock, implying an upside of approximately 33 percent from Monday's closing price. Jefferies has a Buy rating with a target of Rs 2,150, while Goldman Sachs and Citi have targets of Rs 2,010 and Rs 1,940, respectively.
Paytm's parent company, One 97 Communications , closed at Rs 1,654.70 on Monday, gaining 2.4 percent ahead of its earnings announcement. The stock has risen 28.1 percent so far in 2026, outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined 13 percent over the same period. The company's market capitalisation stood at Rs 1.06 lakh crore.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
Bernstein highlighted Paytm’s strong revenue momentum and improving payment margins. The brokerage said that financial services revenue grew 49 percent year-on-year, while marketing services revenue increased 26 percent. Net payment revenue rose 7 percent sequentially and 8 percent year-on-year. Although indirect costs increased 14 percent, EBITDA jumped 90 percent year-on-year, delivering a margin of around 10 percent.
Jefferies cited sustained business momentum and operating efficiencies. The brokerage said Paytm's EBITDA margin improved sharply to 10 percent, while profit before tax exceeded its estimates by 17 percent. However, profit after tax, excluding exceptional items, was in line with expectations because of higher taxes. Jefferies expects the introduction of UPI MDR after Diwali to support profitability, alongside continued growth in loan distribution and investments.
Citi substantially raised its target price on Paytm stock, citing strong growth and improving margins ahead of the proposed UPI MDR implementation. The brokerage expects accelerating growth in financial services and improving net payment margins, even excluding the potential UPI benefit. It also highlighted Paytm's increasing investments in artificial intelligence, marketing and distribution to support customer acquisition and expansion.
Goldman Sachs maintained its Buy rating but lowered its target price, even as it described Paytm's second-quarter performance as better than expected. The brokerage highlighted strong market-share gains, revenue growth and improving margins. It estimates that the recently announced UPI MDR could increase Paytm's EBITDA by up to 40 percent, a potential benefit it believes is not fully reflected in the stock price. Goldman Sachs also sees further earnings opportunities from the expansion of Paytm Postpaid and a potential relaunch of its wallet business.
Paytm reported a net profit of Rs 226 crore for Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 21 crore a year earlier, while revenue rose 28.5 percent to Rs 2,648 crore. EBITDA increased 91.5 percent to Rs 270 crore, with margins improving to 10.2 percent from 6.8 percent.
Paytm expects the proposed UPI MDR, scheduled for implementation after Diwali, to improve its overall payment processing margin by approximately 2.5 basis points. The company expects the impact to stabilise within two to three quarters after implementation.

 Dalmia Bharat shares hit 4-year low after weak Q2 earnings.
 Company posted net loss of Rs 205 cr on exceptional expenses.
 Multiple brokerages trimmed target prices following results.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Shares of Dalmia Bharat today fell to an over four-year low of Rs 1,507.70 on the National Stock Exchange after the cement make posted a weak set of earnings for the July-September quarter of the financial year 2026-27. The company's performance was hit by exceptional expenses, higher input costs and muted volume growth, prompting six brokerages to cut their target prices.
 Dalmia Bharat share price: Cement stock falls to four-year low 
Dalmia Bharat shares opened at Rs 1,545 on NSE and fell 7.2 percent to touch an intra-day low of Rs 1,507.70. At around 12.50 pm, the stock was trading 5.49 percent lower at 1536.50.
Several brokerages expressed concerns over the company's near-term profitability, cost pressures and losses in market share. HSBC downgraded the stock to 'Hold' from its earlier rating, while Morgan Stanley maintained an Underweight stance. On the other hand, Citi, CLSA, Jefferies and Prabhudas Lilladher retained positive ratings but lowered their target prices.
Dalmia Bharat Ltd a consolidated net loss of Rs 205 crore in the September quarter of FY27. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 239 crore in the July-September period of the previous fiscal year, according to a regulatory filing.
Revenue from operations rose 4.27 per cent to Rs 3,563 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 3,417 crore in the year-ago period.
Dalmia Bharat reported exceptional expenses of Rs 339 crore during the quarter, related to the acquisition of Jaiprakash Associates Ltd's cement business, impairment of assets and a voluntary separation scheme for employees.
"During the September quarter, the company recognised an impairment loss of Rs 282 crore on three captive power plants, reflecting the increasing share of lower-cost renewable energy sources, and on a brand discontinued by the group. It also incurred a one-time charge of Rs 57 crore for implementing a separation scheme for eligible employees at select units," it said.
It reported profit before exceptional items and tax of Rs 46 crore, down 85.53 per cent YoY. It was Rs 318 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal year.
"EBITDA stood at Rs 493 crore, impacted by cost headwinds," the company said in its earnings statement.
Dalmia Bharat's sales volume rose 3 per cent to 7.1 million tonnes (MT) during the September quarter.
Total expenses of Dalmia Bharat in the September quarter were at Rs 3,563 crore, up 12.57 per cent year-on-year.
Total income, which includes other income, was at Rs 3,609 crore in the second quarter of FY27, up 3.61 per cent year-on-year.
In the first half (H1), consolidated income of Dalmia Bharat was up 6.55 per cent at Rs 7,638 crore.
 HSBC on Dalmia Bharat: Hold, cuts share price target to Rs 1,820 
Brokerage firm HSBC downgraded Dalmia Bharat to 'Hold' and cut its target price to Rs 1,820 per share. The brokerage cited muted volume growth, large cost increases and asset impairment drive net loss as key factors behind the company's weak numbers in the Q2FY27. It also expects the acquired assets to remain a drag on profitability in the October-December quarter (Q3 FY27), with breakeven targeted by the end of FY27.
 Morgan Stanley on Dalmia Bharat: Underweight, target price Rs 1,640 
Morgan Stanley gave 'Underweight' rating on Dalmia Bharat with a target price of Rs 1,640 per share. The brokerage described the September-quarter results as very weak, citing volume pressures, partly due to seasonality, and elevated cost metrics.
Though operating leverage benefits are expected to support performance in the second half of FY27, Morgan Stanley expects variable costs to stay elevated, partly offsetting the benefits of recent cement price hikes.
The brokerage retained its relatively underweight stance, citing weak profitability.
 CITI on Dalmia Bharat: Retains ‘Buy’, cut target price to Rs 1900 
Citi retained its 'Buy' rating on Dalmia Bharat but trimmed its target price to Rs 1,900 from Rs 2,150. The brokerage stated Q2 EBITDA fell 29 percent YoY to around Rs 490 crore, approximately 3 percent below its estimates. Higher costs, which rose 9 percent, offset the benefits of 3 percent volume growth and a 1 percent improvement in realisations.
Adjusted EBITDA per tonne stood at Rs 694, against Rs 1,055 in Q1 and Rs 1,010 last year. The QoQ EBITDA decline reflected lower realisations, higher costs, lower volumes and losses associated with the Jaiprakash Associates cement assets.
Citi also noted that the company's net debt-to-EBITDA ratio increased to 2x from 1.5 x in the previous quarter.

ITC Hotels share price rose nearly 5% after Jefferies maintains 'buy' rating with a target price at Rs 220/share. Ather Energy shares extended their rally on Tuesday, rising 4 percent in early trade after surging more than 14 percent in the previous session. Brokerages Nomura and HSBC raised their price targets following the electric two-wheeler maker's strong fiscal second quarter earnings.
 Ather Energy stock was trading at Rs 1,638 in early deals, gaining 4 percent and ranking among the top gainers on the BSE 500 and NSE 500 indices. The stock was also among the most actively traded counters on both exchanges.
The stock has surged 121 percent so far in 2026, sharply outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined 13 percent during the same period. Ather Energy's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs 65,000 crore.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
Nomura maintained its 'Buy' rating on Ather Energy and raised its price target to Rs 2,070 from Rs 1,926, implying an upside potential of 31 percent from Monday's closing price. The brokerage reaffirmed Ather Energy as its top pick in the electric two-wheeler segment, citing stronger growth visibility with Konarc, better-than-expected average selling prices (ASPs) and margins in Q2, and robust bookings.
Nomura said the drivers for an inflection in electric vehicle demand were in place. It also said that future stock returns would increasingly depend on the importance of electric vehicles in original equipment manufacturers' (OEMs) businesses.
HSBC also maintained its 'Buy' recommendation and raised its price target to Rs 1,800 from Rs 1,600 following Ather Energy's stronger-than-expected quarterly performance. The brokerage highlighted the company's surprise EBITDA break-even amid challenging commodity cost conditions. It said the operational resilience should strengthen market confidence in Ather Energy's ability to scale its business over the long term.
HSBC now expects the company to achieve profit-after-tax break-even in FY27. However, it flagged a potentially muted market response to Ather Energy's new product, Konarc, as a near-term risk.
Ather Energy reported a net profit of Rs 1.26 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, compared with a loss of Rs 154 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from operations jumped 63 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,464 crore from Rs 899 crore. EBITDA stood at Rs 74.2 crore, marking the company's second consecutive EBITDA-positive quarter, against a loss of Rs 90.7 crore a year earlier. EBITDA margin improved to 4.9 percent from a negative 10 percent.
The company's board approved capital expenditure of Rs 122 crore to expand manufacturing capacity at its Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra facilities. Ather Energy plans to add 75,000 units of annual capacity at its Hosur factory by December 2026, involving investment of up to Rs 58 crore. It also plans to add 1.5 lakh units of annual capacity at its Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar facility by Q2FY28, at an estimated investment of up to Rs 64 crore.

 Stock market recap: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty ended largely unchanged in volatile trade on Tuesday as profit-taking in IT and blue-chip banking stocks, high crude oil prices and caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision kept investors on edge.
 The Sensex fell 8.08 points, or 0.01%, to close at 73,598.67, while the Nifty shed 3.45 points, or 0.02%, to settle at 22,749.75.
 Broader markets, however, outperformed the benchmarks on strong buying interest. The BSE smallcap index rose 2.59%, while the midcap index gained nearly 1%. Sector-wise, realty, pharma and auto stocks advanced, while banking, financial services and IT shares declined.
 Among Sensex constituents, State Bank of India, Axis Bank, Tata Consultancy Services, Asian Paints, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank were among the major laggards. Bharti Airtel, Trent, Maruti Suzuki and Power Grid were among the top gainers.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: Tips Music Ltd (current price: ₹ 741.6) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong monetization of its extensive music catalog through rising digital streaming, YouTube, OTT, and licensing revenues, creating a scalable royalty-led business model. Growing demand for music licensing, synchronization rights, and regional content across digital platforms supports long-term royalty income growth. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 40.13, 52-week high: ₹ 785.00, volume: ₹ 34.76 crore 
 Technical analysis: Consolidation-based pattern breakout 
 Risk factors: High dependence on digital platforms and changing royalty-sharing policies could impact revenue realization from content monetization. Intense competition from major music labels and the need for sustained content acquisition may pressure market share and margins. 
 Buy: ₹ 734–745 
 Target price: ₹ 860 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 699 
 Buy: Acutaas Chemicals Ltd (current price: ₹ 3,793) 
 Why it’s recommended: Expanding presence in high-value specialty chemicals, semiconductor chemicals, battery materials, and pharma intermediates diversifies revenue streams and improves growth visibility. Strong R&D capabilities, a global customer base, and growing CDMO opportunities position the company to benefit from import substitution and demand in specialty chemical. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 70.78, 52-week high: ₹ 3,900.00, volume: ₹ 1,736.95 crore 
 Technical analysis: T-consolidation-based pattern breakout 
 Risk factors: Significant exposure to pharmaceutical and specialty chemical end-markets makes earnings vulnerable to demand slowdown, regulatory issues, or customer concentration. Execution risks in scaling new businesses such as semiconductors, battery chemicals, and CDMO projects could affect profitability and return ratios. 
 Buy at: ₹ 3,755–3,812 
 Target price: ₹ 4,200 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 3,600 
 How Nifty 50 performed 
 Indian equity markets ended Tuesday on a mixed note, with the Nifty 50 slipping 3.45 points, or 0.02%, to close at 22,749.75 after a volatile session. The index opened at 22,708.80, touched an intraday high of 22,829.75 and a low of 22,636.85, before recovering from lower levels towards the close.
 Broader market sentiment remained positive, with 2,455 stocks advancing, 1,103 declining and 107 unchanged, translating into an advance-decline ratio of 2.23:1. Sectoral gains were led by Media (3.66%), Realty (1.94%), Pharma (1.91%), Healthcare (1.65%) and Auto (1.48%). However, losses in Private Banks (0.73%), Financial Services (0.59%) and IT (0.26%) weighed on the benchmark.
 Technical outlook 
 The Nifty 50 formed a small bullish candle on the daily chart, indicating buying interest at lower levels despite continued volatility. The broader technical structure remains cautious, with the index trading below key medium- and long-term moving averages and a descending trendline, suggesting the prevailing downtrend remains intact despite recent recovery attempts. However, the index has reclaimed its short-term moving average near 22,700, pointing to early signs of stabilization.
 The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has recovered to 46, above its signal average of 42.25, indicating improving momentum, although it remains below the neutral 50 mark. The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) has also registered a bullish crossover, with the MACD line at -146.04 moving above the signal line at -196.84. The positive histogram points to strengthening upward momentum.
 Key levels to watch 
 The Nifty 50 rebounded sharply from intraday lows and closed above its 21-day moving average, signalling renewed buying interest and improving near-term sentiment.
 On the downside, 22,500–22,400 remains a key support zone. A decisive break below this range could trigger fresh selling pressure, pulling the index towards 22,200–22,000. On the upside, the 23,000–23,200 range is likely to act as a significant resistance zone following the recent breakdown from these levels.
 How did the Nifty Bank perform? 
 The Nifty Bank underperformed the broader market on Tuesday, falling 391.80 points, or 0.72%, to close at 53,974.90, just above its intraday low of 53,951.20. Selling in private-sector heavyweights outweighed gains in state-run lenders, dragging the index below 54,000 in the final hour as investors stayed cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision on Wednesday.
 ICICI Bank, down 1.2%, was the biggest drag, while HDFC Bank and Axis Bank each fell more than 1%. SBI declined about 1.6%, and IndusInd Bank lost around 1.3%. AU Small Finance Bank extended it

 Bajaj Finance, HDFC Bank , Maruti Suzuki, HCL Technologies and Power Grid were among the laggards.

docs.title: Defence stocks to buy: Systematix initiates coverage for Astra Microwave, Data Patterns, sees up to 66% upside
docs.text:
The brokerage has set a target price of ₹ 2,600 for Astra Microwave against its closing price of ₹ 1569.75, indicating an upside potential of almost 66%. Meanwhile, Data Patterns has a target of ₹ 5,100 against ₹ 4127.90, implying an upside of 23.5%. Systematix Research said the two companies were positioned to benefit from rising demand for radar, electronic warfare, communications and space-related systems. It highlighted their indigenous design capabilities, research and development investments, and opportunities arising from new defence programmes. The brokerage described Astra Microwave as a company undergoing a structural transformation, while identifying Data Patterns as a capability leader among private defence manufacturers. Both companies could see stronger order inflows and earnings growth as existing programmes move towards execution. Astra Microwave has expanded beyond its traditional radio-frequency component business into a broader systems and development-cum-production partner for aerospace, defence and space platforms. Its order book tripled over three years to approximately ₹ 43 billion, providing visibility for future revenue. “ASTM is at an inflection point of an unprecedented structural transformation. Over the past three decades, the company has evolved from a sub-tier radio frequency (RF) component supplier into a Tier-1 Systems and Development-cum-Production Partner (DcPP), with presence across India's critical aerospace, defence, and space platforms. Over the last three years, the company tripled its order book, while improving margins,” said the brokerage. The company received an order worth around ₹ 22 billion in July 2026 for the AAAU unit of the Uttam radar for the Tejas Mk-1A aircraft. Its prospective programmes include airborne radars for Super Sukhoi and Tejas Mk-1A, missile systems such as QRSAM and Akash, and tactical software-defined radios. Systematix Research noted that Astra Microwave was moving towards higher-value subsystems, integration and proprietary intellectual property rather than lower-margin build-to-print contracts. Its consolidated gross margin improved from approximately 30% in FY22 to 51% in FY26, while its EBITDA margin increased from around 12% to 29% over the same period. The brokerage said the proposed separation of Astra Microwave’s space, meteorology and hydrology businesses could also unlock value as the company expands its satellite manufacturing capabilities. Limited competition in most of these projects should help sustain gross margins, with operating leverage expected to drive EBITDA margin, it added. Data Patterns, meanwhile, is expected to benefit from its focus on indigenous design and its expanding presence in airborne, space and counter-drone platforms. Its capabilities span radar, electronic warfare and avionics, supported by a large private-sector research and development team. The company had an order book of ₹ 26.4 billion, including negotiated orders, and management expected an additional ₹ 20 billion of orders in FY27. Systematix also highlighted opportunities in jammer pods for the Su-30 MKI upgrade and counter-drone systems as potential drivers of future order inflows. Systematix Research highlighted Data Patterns’ “largest private sector R&D team” as a key competitive advantage. The brokerage believes its design capabilities and expanding product portfolio position it to benefit from the increasing demand for indigenous defence electronics. Systematix expects Astra Microwave’s revenue to rise from ₹ 11.63 billion in FY26 to ₹ 23.92 billion in FY29, implying a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 27%. Its EBITDA is projected to increase from ₹ 2.69 billion to ₹ 7.83 billion over the same period, while adjusted profit after tax (PAT) is estimated to grow from ₹ 1.93 billion to ₹ 5.22 billion. The brokerage expects order inflows of approximately ₹ 90 billion for Astra Microwave over FY27-FY29, supported by radar, missile and communication programmes. It has assigned a BUY rating and a target price of ₹ 2,600, based on a sum-of-the-parts valuation. For Data Patterns, Systematix projects revenue, EBITDA and PAT to grow at CAGRs of 29%, 32% and 32%, respectively, between FY26 and FY29. The anticipated increase in order inflows and a shift towards higher-volume production are expected to support growth from FY28. Systematix Research said: “Revenue growth is expected to accelerate from FY28,” reflecting the anticipated transition towards higher-volume execution at Data Patterns. For Zydus Lifesciences futures, he suggests an entry range of ₹ 1,170– ₹ 1,180, with targets of ₹ 1,250– ₹ 1,300 and a stop-loss below ₹ 1,130. He also recommends buying Sun Pharmaceutical Industries futures at ₹ 1,760– ₹ 1,770, with targets of ₹ 1,840– ₹ 1,880 and a stop-loss below ₹ 1,730. Jay Thakkar, Vice President and Head of Derivatives and Quantitative Research at ICICI Securities, said the Nifty 50 closed almost flat on monthly expiry day after facing selling pressure at higher levels. The index attempted to move above 22,800 towards 23,000 but failed to sustain the gains. It also briefly slipped below 22,700, reflecting intraday volatility. However, India VIX declined nearly 5%, indicating that volatility remained relatively contained. Thakkar said the market has been trading in a range ahead of key global and domestic events, including the Federal Reserve’s policy decision, GDP data and geopolitical developments. He noted that the Nifty 50’s immediate trading range is 22,000–23,000, with a decisive breakout on either side likely to determine the next directional move. Until then, the index is expected to remain range-bound, with India VIX likely to trade between 15 and 20. On the Bank Nifty, Thakkar said the index has underperformed the Nifty 50 in recent sessions. He identified 53,000 as a crucial support and 56,000 as a key resistance, putting the index in a trading range of 53,000–56,000. A breakout beyond either level could signal the next move. Within the banking space, he expects private sector banks to outperform public sector banks. Jay Thakkar of ICICI Securities recommends Central Depository Services Ltd ( CDSL ) Futures, Zydus Lifesciences Futures, and Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Futures. According to Axis Securities' Top Dividend Yield Stocks report dated October 26, 2026, PTC India topped the small-cap list with a dividend yield of 24%, followed by CESC at 10%. Among large-cap stocks, Vedanta and Coal India recorded dividend yields of 7% each, while Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) led the public sector undertaking ( PSU ) category with a yield of 7%. Dividends are payments that companies distribute to shareholders from their profits or accumulated reserves, subject to applicable rules and corporate decisions. They can provide investors with an additional source of income alongside any potential appreciation in share prices. Dividend yield measures the annual dividend paid per share as a percentage of its current market price. For example, if a stock trades at ₹ 100 and pays an annual dividend of ₹ 5 per share, its dividend yield is 5%. PTC India topped Axis Securities' small-cap dividend yield list, with a reported yield of 24%. The company had a market capitalisation of ₹ 3,960 crore and a share price of ₹ 134. It paid dividends of ₹ 31.5 per share over the preceding 12 months. CESC ranked second, with a dividend yield of 10%, a share price of ₹ 124 and a market capitalisation of ₹ 16,495 crore. It paid ₹ 12 per share in dividends during the same period. Other small-cap companies featuring in the list included Brookfield India Real Estate Trust and Gateway Distriparks, both with dividend yields of 7%. docs.text:
JSW Steel is the brokerage’s preferred long-term compounder, backed by consistent capacity additions, while SAIL offers a margin recovery opportunity. Aditya Birla Money has set a target price of ₹ 1,425 for JSW Steel, implying an 18% upside from its current market price of ₹ 1,220 as of 22 October. For SAIL, the brokerage has set a target price of ₹ 225, indicating a potential upside of 36.8% from ₹ 170. For international investors, the brokerage has initiated coverage on ArcelorMittal with a Positive view. It highlighted the company's ambition to expand its capacity in India to 40 million tonnes from the current 9 million tonnes. The global steel cycle is strengthening as protectionist policies reshape trade flows and reduce the influence of cross-border import parity pricing, Aditya Birla Money said. Measures such as the European Union's tariff-rate quotas, Section 232 tariffs in the US and India's safeguard duty are supporting regional pricing power. The brokerage believes concerns that India's 11–12% safeguard duty will be withdrawn in 2028 may be overstated. It expects the measures to remain in place beyond 2028, supported by policy continuity and protectionist measures across major steel-consuming economies. In its assessment, the current rally is being driven by structural policy changes rather than temporary factors, potentially making the favourable pricing environment more durable than investors expect. The brokerage's proprietary steel supply-demand model points to a tightening domestic market. It assumes Indian steel consumption will grow at a 7.5% compound annual growth rate, while supply from major producers expands at a measured pace. Based on its estimates, domestic steel inventories could decline from around 10 million tonnes currently to almost zero over the next three years, even as supply and demand both grow by approximately 6–8% annually. The expected inventory drawdown could keep steel prices above their 10-year averages, although short-term inventory movements may lead to volatility. The brokerage’s preferred exposure is therefore through JSW Steel for its capacity-led growth and through SAIL for its margin-recovery potential. Tata Steel and Jindal Steel remain additional picks, while ArcelorMittal offers a longer-term international investment opportunity linked to its planned expansion in India. docs.title: No purchase bill for inherited gold? Here's how to calculate tax
docs.text:
Mint Money No purchase bill for inherited gold? Here's how to calculate tax Aprajita Sharma 3 min read 27 Oct 2026, 01:01 PM IST Summary Inherited jewellery may be tax-free when received, but selling it can trigger capital gains tax. The acquisition cost, holding period and sale price determine the tax bill. Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now Suppose you are rummaging through your old almirah and stumble upon a couple of pieces of jewellery your grandmother gifted you when you were a child. You need money for an important expense and decide to sell one of them. You know that gifts received from specified relatives, such as parents, grandparents or spouses, are tax-free at the time of receipt. But will the capital gains from selling the jewellery also be tax-free? Not really. The tax liability will depend on the cost of acquisition, the holding period and the sale price. The date you inherited or received the jewellery as a gift will not determine the tax treatment on its own. The previous owner’s cost of acquisition and holding period, along with the date of sale, will come into the picture. “In the case of inherited gold, the previous owner's holding period is included when determining whether the asset qualifies as long-term. It does not matter when the seller became the owner of the asset,” said CA Ashish Karundia. Finding the cost This brings up another challenge: how do you establish the previous owner’s cost of acquisition? Since the jewellery may be decades old, you may not have the original purchase bill. What can you do in such a situation? “The absence of the original purchase bill does not mean that the entire sale value becomes taxable. If it is unavailable, one can use other evidence, such as valuation reports, jeweller records or other documents, to substantiate the cost,” said Karundia. You could approach the original jeweller, if identifiable, or a valuation professional to establish the acquisition cost. However, if the jewellery was acquired before 1 April 2001, you may opt to use its fair market value (FMV) as on that date instead of its actual cost of acquisition. “For gold acquired before 1 April 2001, the fair market value as on that date can be considered,” said Karundia. How much tax will you pay? Physical gold is treated as a capital asset. For gold sold on or after 23 July 2024, it qualifies as a long-term capital asset if the holding period exceeds 24 months. Long-term capital gains are taxed at 12.5% without indexation, while short-term capital gains are taxed at the applicable income-tax slab rate. The taxable capital gain can be reduced by deducting the eligible cost of acquisition and qualifying expenses incurred wholly and exclusively in connection with the sale. “There is no specific capital gains exemption merely because the gold is inherited or constitutes family jewellery. However, eligible transfer-related expenses, such as a commission paid to an intermediary for arranging the sale, can be deducted while calculating capital gains,” said Karundia. Suppose you sell inherited jewellery in 2026 for ₹ 15 lakh. You establish that your grandmother acquired it before 1 April 2001 and opt to use its FMV on that date, which is ₹ 1.5 lakh. You also pay a commission of ₹ 15,000 to an intermediary who facilitates the sale. To calculate your long-term capital gain, deduct the eligible cost of acquisition of ₹ 1.5 lakh and the sales commission of ₹ 15,000 from the sale proceeds of ₹ 15 lakh. This brings the taxable capital gain to ₹ 13.35 lakh. At the applicable long-term capital gains tax rate of 12.5%, the tax liability works out to ₹ 1,66,875. Add health and education cess of 4%, amounting to ₹ 6,675, and the total tax payable comes to ₹ 1,73,550, or approximately ₹ 1.74 lakh. Can you claim an exemption? Individuals selling gold at a long-term capital gain may also explore the exemption under Section 54F of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (Section 86 under the Income-tax Act, 2025), subject to the applicable provisions and conditions. “The exemption may be available if the net sale consideration is invested in a residential house in India within the prescribed timelines and other eligibility requirements are met,” said Karundia. docs.title: NPS charges: PFRDA postpones implementation of revised PoP fee structure to December 1; what subscribers should know
docs.text:
The revised structure, announced on August 28, 2026, provides for a one-time onboarding charge of ₹ 200 per Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) and an annual charge of 0.20% of assets under management (AUM) across all NPS schemes. In its circular released on October 26, 2026, PFRDA mentioned that “the date of implementation of the revised charge structure specified therein, which was earlier prescribed as 01.10.2026, stands revised to 01.12.2026.” It further stated, “Accordingly, the Central Recordkeeping Agencies (CRAs) shall implement the revised charge structure for deduction of applicable charges with effect from 01.12.2026.” Here is what the change means for NPS subscribers. Points of Presence (PoPs) are authorised intermediaries that help subscribers access NPS services, including account opening and contributions. Central Recordkeeping Agencies (CRAs) maintain subscriber records and process related transactions, including the deduction of applicable charges. NPS-Lite was launched in 2010 to provide affordable pension coverage to unorganised-sector workers, with government co-contributions under the Swavalamban scheme. Only Gramin Dak Sevaks (GDS) of the Department of Posts are allowed to enrol in NPS-Lite, as fresh enrolments were discontinued after the launch of the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) in 2015. Under the 2018 PoP Regulations, PFRDA regulates the charges that Points of Presence (PoPs) can collect from subscribers. Following the removal of the distinction between Common Schemes and schemes introduced under the Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF), the regulator revised the PoP fee structure for NPS and NPS Lite schemes in its August 28, 2026, circular. The revised charges are as follows: No. Subscribers onboarded through e-NPS who make subsequent contributions through e-NPS or D-Remit will not be liable to pay PoP charges. However, subscribers onboarded through a PoP will remain liable for the prescribed charges even if they subsequently contribute through e-NPS or D-Remit. According to PFRDA, a dormant account is one linked to a unique PAN across all CRAs in which no contribution is made for four consecutive quarters, as identified at the end of each quarter. Such accounts will not attract annual charges. The circular also specifies minimum contributions of ₹ 250 at onboarding and ₹ 10 for subsequent contributions under NPS. The revised charges will take effect from December 1, 2026, rather than October 1. Subscribers should check the PoP’s revised fees before opening an account. According to the circular, PoPs must display their updated charge structures on their websites and clearly communicate the applicable charges to subscribers through pop-up notifications during digital onboarding.
