docs.title: Jio IPO listing: Buy, Hold or Avoid? Top market experts weigh in
docs.text: Is Jio ‘overpriced’ or a ‘long-term Buy’? The Street is waiting with bated breath to see if the listing of the Mukesh Ambani-led telecom major ring in Diwali early on D’Street. The GMP has been holding steady around 22%. Most market observers see it fairly valued at current levels and are betting on the long-term prospects of the telecom sector in India. Here is a quick look at how leading market gurus value Jio Platforms and expectations going forward. ‘Jio, Airtel among the top telecom picks’ Speaking on the possible listing price, market veteran Arun Kejriwal pointed out that “the subscription tells you that the demand that has been generated is far greater than what people were talking about. Very clearly, this means that people have liked the story of Jio, and therefore they have subscribed. If I were to hazard a guess, the price on listing day may move within a band of Rs 1,330 to 1,380 a share.” Speaking on the broad prospects of the telecom sector and top picks in that space, he added that “from a comparable perspective with Airtel, which is the competitor, it has a larger subscriber base or user base, and they are the youngest telecom company in the country, having finished the first decade. So Jio and Airtel would be vying for investors' money, and of course the other two stocks, Bharti Hexacom and Vodafone Idea, would be a distant third or fourth, respectively.” ALSO READJio Platforms IPO Listing Live Updates: Big debut or a surprise? Check GMP, share price ‘Valuations attractive, see pricing discipline ahead’ Interestingly, the grey market premium for the Jio IPO sustained through the IPO bidding period and has seen significant interest from retail and HNI investors. Sandip Sabharwal of Asksandipsabharwal.com believes that the real story is in the pricing. “Given that it was not very aggressively priced, it got a very good response. I think the main reasons are that investors believe that going forward there will be greater pricing discipline once Jio gets listed and ARPUs for the entire industry are likely to move up.” Overall he thinks “the stock is cheap relative to historic valuations as well as what they are doing and the kind of earning growth potential that's there. Obviously if the listing is good and the stock does well post-listing, it will have a positive rub-off effect on the Reliance Industries stock too.” Expect Jio market cap to double in 4-5 years The Jio Platforms issue is not just the largest IPO in India’s primary market history but also set to command a significant market cap post-listing. Deven R Choksey, Founder and MD of DRChoksey Finserv believes that the telecom play may see its market cap double in 5 years, “We will have to be careful about the hype which is getting created during the listing and post listing. I think for long-term investment, you have to be completely convincing. I maintain that in 4.5 to 5 years, the market cap of 10 lakh crore at the IPO is expected to double. So, Jio in most likelihood, I think, would be the second company after Reliance as far as the market cap size is concerned. So, if number one is Reliance industry, number two would be Jio as far as market capitalisation is concerned, post listing.” Jio: ‘Valuations cheap, expect listing-day pop’ Most market observers have given a thumbs up to Jio’s valuations. Market veteran Ambareesh Baliga expects a definite pop on listing day because “in the short-term on listing, yes, there will be a pop-up. And I think it should be about a 10% sort of premium. Valuation-wise, I think they had left some decent amount on the table.” ALSO READMissed Jio IPO allotment? Analysts reveal entry levels for the telecom stock after listing If you compare with Bharti also, “valuation-wise, it is cheaper. So, there is a gap. The sort of response which they got was much better than what was expected, especially on the institutional side. We need to see whether the institutional demand in the IPO gets converted to demand on listing. If that happens, yes, I think we could see the stock possibly holding up or moving up from there. But then, if you're talking of long-term, I think this sector is surely going to outperform,” he added. Dipan Mehta, Director of Elixir Equities, corroborated that view and said that “The price at which the issue has been done is very well priced, in fact slightly underpriced as well at a discount to its closest competitor and peer-to-peer company, Bharti Airtel by at least about 20 to 25 percent. You could expect anywhere from Rs 150 to Rs 250 pop on listing.” Sneha Poddar, Vice President of Research at Wealth Management firm Motilal Oswal too anticipates “a strong listing-day performance for Jio Platforms, underpinned by robust institutional interest and a tightly constrained initial free float of around 3%, which creates favourable supply-demand dynamics. Furthermore, anticipation of imminent telecom tariff revisions provides positive near-term momentum.” She pointed out that, “Jio is a compelling long-term accumulation, priced at roughly 11.2x FY28E EV/EBITDA, its valuation is well-supported by industry-leading operating metrics, including 50% plus EBITDA margins, dominant market share in wireless and broadband, and a structural path toward robust cash-flow compounding.” Betting on long-term fundamentals Overall, most market participants seem almost certain of a 10% kind of pop at debut. Importantly, they believe it will be interesting to see how the Jio Platform stock holds up post listing. Most see it as a key telecom player at a significant discount to its closest peer, Bharti Airtel with room for adequate upside ahead. docs.title: IDFC First to IndusInd Bank: Nomura picks 3 bank stocks for up to 33% upside
docs.text: Japanese brokerage Nomura remains bullish on the Indian banking sector and has ‘Buy’ calls on three banks with up to 33% upside. The brokerage has raised earnings estimates for these banks, factoring in 50 basis points of repo rate hikes, the implementation of expected credit loss framework from April, and the cap on insurance distribution commissions. Here are the three banks with a ‘Buy’ recommendation from Nomura - Nomura on Kotak Mahindra Bank Nomura has a ‘Buy’ call on Kotak Mahindra with a target price of Rs 500, implying an upside of 13% from the current price of Rs 442 apiece. ALSO READ7x earnings, a 59% fall: Vijay Kedia and Dolly Khanna’s latest smallcap bets The bank delivered a steady quarter, with growth in net interest income. It mobilised around Rs 55,300 crore of FCNR (B) deposits, or 8% of its total deposits. “Of this, it lent INR161bn (Rs 16,100 crore) against these deposits through its international branches and used part to fund the ~INR96bn (Rs 9,600 crore) KMIL book. Management expects to deploy the remaining liquidity into customer assets over the next few quarters,” Nomura said. The brokerage raised its FY27 loan growth view to 25% from 17% and deposit growth forecast to 24% from 15%. Nomura on IDFC First Bank The Japanese brokerage maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 95, implying an upside of nearly 33% from the current price of Rs 71.54 apiece. IDFC First Bank delivered a strong Q2FY27, with its net profit exceeding Nomura’s estimates. The brokerage raised its FY27 earnings per share (EPS) estimate by 5% and FY28 EPS estimate by 2% and expects loan growth of 30% in FY27. “Our estimates factor in the impact of the draft insurance commission norms, which take FY28F core fees down 8%,” it said. The bank’s management expects net interest margins (NIM) to recover to 5.8% by Q4FY27 as liquidity is deployed and repo hikes pass through, with 32-33% of the loan book repo-linked. “It also expects the FY28F hit from the draft insurance commission norms to be broadly offset by cheaper FCNR(B) funding (~1% below domestic deposits) and repo hikes.” Nomura on IndusInd Bank The brokerage has a ‘Buy’ rating on IndusInd Bank with a target price of Rs 1,060, implying an upside of nearly 25% from the current price of RS 848.60 apiece. During Q2FY27, the positives for the bank were the micro loan book, which grew 8% sequentially to Rs 17,600 crore after nearly eight quarters of decline. Vehicle finance grew only 1% sequentially, while personal loans and credit cards continued to shrink. “Reported NIM fell 34bp q-q to 3.23%, or 12bp excluding the 1Q IT refund. About half of the decline came from FCNR(B)-related balance sheet expansion, and management expects to recoup it over the next two quarters through faster retail growth,” Nomura said. ALSO READKotak Mahindra Bank: Why brokerages see up to 21% upside despite 22 bps drop in margins Nomura has raised its FY27 and FY28 EPS estimate by 16% and 7%, respectively, on higher growth and lower credit costs. It has also lifted the loan growth view to 22% from 15%. “Our estimates also factor in a 50bp rate hike by Dec-26, ECL implementation from Apr-27 and the cap on insurance distribution commissions.” Conclusion Nomura remains positive on the Indian banking sector. It raised EPS estimates for all the three banks it has a ‘Buy’ call on, mainly due to higher growth and lower credit costs. It has also raised loan growth and deposit growth forecasts. docs.title: 7x earnings, a 59% fall: Vijay Kedia and Dolly Khanna’s latest smallcap bets
docs.text: Vijay Kedia and Dolly Khanna Go Shopping in the Smallcap Bargain Bin Shareholding data for the September 2026 quarter shows two familiar names going against the market's mood. Vijay Kedia, through his firm Kedia Securities, took a fresh 1.49% stake in Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services. The fintech stock has lost nearly 59% of its value in a year. Dolly Khanna made a quieter move. She is back in Rajshree Polypack, a maker of plastic food packaging, with 1.05%. She had dropped off its shareholder list after March 2025. The stock trades below its book value. On the surface, a software-led payments firm and a plastic cup maker have little in common. But both have been marked down hard, both grew sales at over 20% a year for five years, and both now trade at a lower PE than the median for their industry. The question is whether the market has priced in too much bad news, or not enough. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now #1 Zaggle’s 59% Wipeout: Why Kedia Replaced Kacholia in the September Quarter Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services helps companies manage what their staff spend. It issues prepaid and corporate cards, and runs software for expense claims, vendor payments and employee rewards. As of FY26, it served 3,915 corporate customers and about 39 lakh users. It came to the market in September 2023 at an IPO price of Rs 164. The timing of Kedia's entry is the story. On 17th August 2026, the stock fell 20% after its June quarter profit dropped 33%. On the same day, the company disclosed that its appeal against an income tax demand for AY 2022-23 had been dismissed. The next day, according to bulk deal data on the exchange, Kedia Securities bought 20 lakh shares at Rs 164.72, almost exactly the IPO price, for about Rs 33 cr. These aren’t the first small cap names added to Kedia’s portfolio recently, Recently, I also wrote about 2 more small cap stocks Vijay Kedia invested in, which you must read about. Then came the twist. Ashish Kacholia had held 2.16% of Zaggle in June 2026. In the September filing, his name is missing. Individual holders are named in these filings only once they own 1% or more, so his stake has at least shrunk under that mark. Whether he sold everything is unknown. What is clear is that one well-known smallcap investor reduced his position in the same quarter another chose to buy. Five Years of 50% Sales Growth, But Thinner Margins The long-term growth record is hard to fault. Financial YearFY21FY22FY23FY24FY25FY265Y CAGRSales (Rs cr)2403715537761,3031,85350%EBITDA (Rs cr)2860487111518145%Net Profit (Rs cr)194223448713348% Source: Screener.in EBITDA is operating profit before other income. Sales have grown nearly eight-fold in five years, and profit has grown about seven-fold. The catch is in the margins. Operating margin was 16% in FY22. It has sat at 9 to 10% since. Zaggle earns more as it grows, but it keeps a smaller slice of each rupee. ALSO READVijay Kedia’s latest bets: Rs 73 cr in 2 smallcaps with surging profits The June 2026 quarter made that worse. Sales rose 18% from a year earlier, but net profit fell from Rs 26 cr to Rs 17 cr, and margin slipped to 7%. Management attributed the drop to approximately Rs 3 crore in integration costs for DICE, a newly acquired expense software business—noting that related revenue is only expected to reflect from the September quarter onwards. The deal itself was reworked into an asset purchase for Rs 68 cr, down from Rs 123 cr earlier. Management also kept its FY27 target of about 40% revenue growth. Zaggle is also looking abroad. On 22nd October 2026, it set up a wholly owned subsidiary in the Abu Dhabi Global Market, with a starting capital of USD 10,000. It is a small first step, but it points to Gulf ambitions. The FCF Reality: Profit vs. Cash Conversion The share price of Zaggle was around Rs 158 on its listing day in September 2023 and as of closing on 26th October 2026 it was Rs 152. That is below the IPO price, 73% below its January 2025 peak, and about 9% under what Kedia paid. On valuations, the stock trades at a PE of 17x compared to the current industry median of 20x. Its median PE since listing in 2023 is 65x, while the 10-year industry median is 31x. The stock has gone from one of the priciest names in its group to one of the cheaper ones. Smart money has been leaving. Domestic institutions held 14.56% in December 2024 and just 2.69% by September 2026. Foreign investors fell from 9.17% to 2.49% over the same period. Small shareholders filled the gap. Their number rose 42% to about 1.29 lakh. One more figure deserves attention: free cash flow was negative Rs 113 cr in FY26, so the profits are not yet turning into cash. #2 Rajshree Polypack: Dolly Khanna Returns to a Packaging Stock at 7x Earnings Incorporated in 2011, Rajshree Polypack makes the plastic cups, tubs, lids and sheets that hold your curd, ice cream and takeaway food. Its products also include printed sleeves and moulded parts. Dairy, quick-service restaurants and online food delivery are among the end markets management says are growing. It also runs a paper-based food packaging joint venture, Olive Ecopak. Dolly Khanna has been here before. She held 1.16% in December 2024 and 1.08% in March 2025, then vanished from the list for five quarters. She also returned to Rain Industries in the same quarter, a sign she is revisiting old names rather than chasing new ones. The September 2026 filing shows her back with 7.78 lakh shares, or 1.05%. At the current price, that is worth only about Rs 1.4 cr, a small bet even in her Rs 323 cr portfolio. This addition comes after the brutal clean up Dolly Khanna did in the last quarter. docs.title: Nvidia, AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta: Why the AI infrastructure deal is important
docs.text: Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta Platforms as the Facebook parent steps up its investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure. AMD will also invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering, taking the combined investment from the two chipmakers to $4 billion. The investments come as Meta plans to raise up to $97.5 billion to fund its AI infrastructure expansion. This will be the largest fundraising effort in the Meta's history. Meta announced its fundraising plan on Monday, initially proposing to raise $35 billion through underwritten public equity offerings, followed by another $60 billion through an at-the-market programme. The company subsequently increased its overall fundraising target to $97.5 billion. The funds will support Meta's core business and emerging AI opportunities, including its family of apps, AI models and the infrastructure needed to develop and run them. ALSO READThe volatility of agentic chatter Nvidia and Meta make their AI partnership solid Nvidia said on Monday, October 26, that it would invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering and expand its partnership with the company on Muse, Meta's AI assistant and family of models. The companies will work together to improve the training and inference performance of Muse models. Training involves teaching an AI model to recognise patterns and generate responses. Nvidia said Meta's Muse models and agents use its computing infrastructure and have delivered strong benchmark performance and rising consumer downloads since their launch. Meta also intends to expand its deployment of Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems and Vera central processing units. The company will additionally use Nvidia's Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4 technology to improve network efficiency and support its growing AI workloads. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a press statement, “AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf.” “This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents,” Huang added. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said, “Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We're excited to keep working with NVIDIA to deliver the best personal agents and frontier models for billions of people.” The companies are also considering further collaboration on Nvidia's OpenShell framework, which is designed to support the safe deployment of AI agents, and its Sentry technology for monitoring agent behaviour. ALSO READ‘Data centre in a container’: The multibillion-dollar opportunity and 2 stocks to watch Why Muse is important to Meta's AI plans Muse is central to Zuckerberg's ambition to bring more advanced, personalised AI capabilities to the billions of people who use Meta's services. According to Reuters, the assistant, known internally as Hatch, is modelled on the open-source AI agent OpenClaw. It can access applications covering email, calendars, payments, health, shopping and smart-home services, subject to user permissions that can be revoked. Unlike conventional chatbots that mainly respond to prompts, AI agents are designed to use tools and carry out tasks on behalf of users. Their ability to perform more complex tasks could make them an important part of Meta's Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp ecosystem. Developing these capabilities requires substantial computing power. Meta's expanded partnership with Nvidia is intended to improve model performance while reducing the cost of training and running AI systems. The focus on inference is particularly important as AI services attract more users. Every interaction with an AI assistant requires computing resources, making efficiency a key consideration as usage increases. AMD also invests as chipmakers expand their ties with Meta AMD announced a $1 billion investment in Meta's equity offering, adding a financial commitment to its existing technology partnership with the company. AMD said its Helios racks were already running at Meta, while its EPYC processors were powering Meta's Muse. The company is also working with Meta on infrastructure designed to operate at gigawatt scale. AMD CEO Lisa Su said, “Together, we are building and deploying infrastructure at gigawatt scale and shaping future generations of silicon, software and systems to enable Meta’s most ambitious superintelligence models and services.” Meta had previously said that Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom had expressed interest in purchasing up to $5 billion in shares collectively. The disclosed investments from Nvidia and AMD account for $4 billion of that amount. Why the deal is important for the AI industry The investments show how the relationship between major technology companies and chipmakers is evolving. Nvidia and AMD are not only supplying the processors needed to build AI infrastructure but are also investing in companies that rely on their technology. Nvidia has expanded its investments across the AI industry. According to Dealroom data cited by CNBC, it participated in 121 investment rounds in 2026, compared with 13 in 2022. Its investments include OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel and xAI. AMD has also increased its investment activity, participating in 25 funding rounds in 2026, up from two in 2022. In July, the company said it would make an equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic.

docs.title: Missed Jio IPO allotment? Analysts reveal entry levels for the telecom stock after listing
docs.text: Think of a popular restaurant on a Sunday night. Everyone wants a table, but only a handful get the seats. Something similar has happened with the Jio Platforms IPO. The basis of allotment was finalised on October 26, and some applicants will see shares in their accounts while others will get a refund of their application amount. This leaves investors with one key question - what should they do if they do not receive any shares? With the issue attracting heavy demand, missing out on an allotment does not necessarily mean missing the opportunity to invest. They can buy it from the secondary market after listing. However, buying shares after listing requires a fresh assessment of the price. Market experts have shared the levels they consider reasonable for investors who want to hold the stock over the long term. Jio IPO: What is the entry price if you miss allotment? For investors who do not receive shares through the IPO, the listing price will become an important factor in deciding whether to enter the stock. Dipan Mehta, Director of Elixir Equities, believes investors could consider buying shares around the listing, provided they are prepared to stay invested for the long term. “I think investors should try to average on listing. Up to about Rs 1,300 is a good sort of investment, but you have to have a long-term focus.” ALSO READJio IPO: From 100-minute subscription to Rs 7.4 lakh Cr bids – 5 historic records What makes Jio Platforms a long-term investment bet? Mehta's view is based on the role telecom companies could play as internet usage and technology adoption expand. He sees Jio Platforms as a way to gain exposure to the telecom business and the infrastructure needed to support newer technologies. He said, “It’s a very unique company in the sense that it is one of India’s leading telecom companies, along with Bharti Airtel. Any consumer-facing technology has to be implemented or scaled up, and the infrastructure has to be provided by telecom companies like Bharti Airtel and Jio, not just in terms of 5G but also broadband and future communication-related technologies. So, I’m very positive on the entire sector. It’s a combination of several technologies available in a single stock.” Is it worth buying above the IPO price? Sneha Poddar, VP, Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal, has also indicated that investors with a longer investment horizon could consider entering at levels above the issue price. Poddar said, "From a long-term point of view, IPO price or 5-10% higher levels are also reasonable levels to enter" She also pointed to a possible near-term trigger for the telecom sector, adding "anticipation of imminent telecom tariff revisions provides positive near-term momentum." Jio Platforms IPO: Issue size, subscription and listing date Jio Platforms raised Rs 30,213 crore through its IPO, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870-crore issue in 2024 to become India's largest public issue by value. The IPO opened on October 21 and closed on October 23, with a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. ALSO READJio IPO Allotment Status Live Update: GMP signals 22% listing premium, Steps to check status online The issue received an overall subscription of 22.19 times. Qualified institutional buyers subscribed 70.55 times their allocated portion, while the non-institutional investor category was subscribed 14 times and the retail portion 2.72 times. The basis of allotment is scheduled to be finalised on October 26, while the shares are expected to list on the BSE and NSE on October 28, 2026. Due to low liquidity, investors must be prepared for severe price volatility and material difficulty in exiting the position. docs.title: 15-fold dividend jump, 3.2% yield: A shipping PSU for your 2027 watchlist
docs.text: Welcome to the latest edition of Dividend Hunter. In recent weeks, we have analysed companies where strong cash flows could translate into consistent dividends. In our previous edition, we covered a diversified public sector company that delivered a 3.5% dividend yield. This week, in our Dividend Hunter series, we discuss a Navratna central public sector enterprise. The company is India’s largest shipping enterprise, operating a diverse fleet of 58 owned vessels across crude & product tankers, bulk carriers, container liners, offshore support, and gas transport (LPG/LNG). During the last five financial years, its standalone revenue and net profit grew at a CAGR of 9% and 16% respectively. Over the same period, its share price returned 18% CAGR. In fact, its consolidated net profit grew faster by 62.9% year-on-year to ₹1,326 crore in FY26. For FY26, the company returned 26.3% of Net Profit to shareholders as dividend distributions. Moreover, during the FY24-26 period, its dividend per share (DPS) increased from ₹0.50 to ₹7.50, a 15-fold rise. During this period, the company's total dividend payout increased from ₹23.3 crore to ₹349.4 crore. This surge in payouts occurred as the company nearly doubled its net profit to ₹1,326 crore in FY26. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now The company is Shipping Corporation of India (SCI). Shipping Corporation of India Share Price From ₹0.50 to ₹7.50: How DIPAM Net Worth Rules Unlocked SCI’s 15-Fold Dividend Surge SCI paid a per-share dividend of ₹7.5 in FY26, translating into a dividend yield of 3.2% at the current price (as of October 23) of ₹238. During the year, the company paid two interim dividends totalling ₹6.5 and a final dividend of ₹1.0 per share. Typically, the company pays a dividend every year in September and November. One common pattern is the sharp increase in dividend payouts over the past two years. Between FY22 and FY24, the company distributed just ₹15.4 crore to ₹23.3 crore annually, with its dividend payout ratio remaining below 4%. This changed significantly in FY25, when the dividend per share jumped to ₹6.59 and the total payout rose to ₹307 crore, accounting for 37.7% of net profit. In FY26, the company further increased the dividend per share to ₹7.5, taking the total payout to ₹349.4 crore. However, with net profit rising to ₹1,326 crore, the payout ratio moderated to 26.3%. This indicates that the company has stepped up shareholder returns while retaining a larger share of its earnings to support future growth. Historical Dividend Payout Track Record YearDividend/ShareTotal Dividend(In Crore)Standalone Net Profit (In Crore)Payout RatioFY22₹0.33₹15.4₹790.01.9%FY23₹0.44₹20.5₹800.0~2.6%FY24₹0.50₹23.3₹612.03.8%FY25₹6.59₹307.0₹814.037.7%FY26₹7.50₹349.4₹1,326.026.3%Source: Annual Report, Financialexpress.com Tanker Fleet Delivers 75% Profit Surge as Middle East Route Disruptions Elevate Tonne-Mile Rates In FY26, the company’s standalone revenue from operations grew by 3.3% to ₹5,778.1 crore. The tanker division was the primary driver of growth during the year. Tanker revenue increased by 9.2% year-on-year to ₹3,942.2 crore, while the segment’s profit rose by 74.9% to ₹1,189.5 crore. ALSO READRs 2.35 lakh cr naval push: 2 stocks to watch as India targets 200 warships Profitability was driven by higher freight rates, more time-charter days, and active spot market deployment. Growth was also supported by increased overall tonne-mile demand due to the longer trade route and the Strait of Hormuz blockade. Bulk carrier revenue increased 10.9% year-on-year to ₹788.9 crore, while losses narrowed to ₹19.1 crore from ₹22.2 crore. Revenue improved due to higher voyage charters and better fleet deployment, supported by a 74% higher Baltic Dry Index in the fourth quarter. Revenue from the liner segment declined to ₹784 crore from ₹1,036 crore in the previous year, while segment profit fell to ₹74.84 crore. Lower container freight rates and reduced cargo volumes weighed on the segment’s performance. However, coastal liner services continued to maintain high vessel utilisation, providing some support amid weaker market conditions. Technical and Offshore Support contributed ₹297.9 crore to revenue in FY26. Other income stood at ₹440.2 crore, providing additional support to the overall financial performance. EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation, and Amortisation) grew faster by 45.6% to ₹2,632.9 crore during the year, while margin expanded by 10.5 percentage points to 45.6%. Lower operating expenses (-10.8%), a shift in revenue-mix towards the higher-margin tanker business, an increase in other income (+128%) and a reduction in bulk carrier losses helped improve margins. This operational leverage pushed Standalone net profit up 62.9% to ₹1,326 crore. SCI returned 26.3% of this net profit to shareholders as dividends. In addition to the year's standalone net profit, the Board evaluates retained earnings, projected cash flows, working capital requirements, debt maturity profile, capex freight and charter hire rates, and debt servicing agreements before declaring a dividend. Higher Freight Rates Acting as a Tailwind For instance, during FY26, higher time-charter rates and spot freight rate spikes during Middle East trade disruptions boosted the company profitability. This prompted the board to deliver higher dividend per share and total payout even though the payout ratio declined. For FY27, the outlook also remains favourable for tanker operators. Freight rates are still higher supported by ongoing geopolitical disruptions, longer shipping routes and tight effective vessel availability. SCI reported a revenue growth of 40.2% year-on-year to ₹1,845 crore in Q1FY27. Q1FY27 Profit Doubles to ₹664 Crore: Cyclical Peak or Sustainable Cash Engine? docs.title: Dalal Street Diwali sale: Kotak adds 5 midcaps with up to 37% upside — Full list
docs.text: Every Diwali, shoppers hunt for the best deals. Sale boards go up. Bags fill fast. Now imagine the same scene on Dalal Street, India’s stock market hub. The shares have seen sharp correction lately. Is this a warning sign or time for some bargain buying in the stock market? Kotak Institutional Equities, a brokerage firm in its report dated October 26 has a fresh shopping list. After the recent correction, several shares are trading below their earlier levels, prompting investors to look for value rather than chase rising prices. Kotak Institutional Equities has reshuffled its recommended portfolios ahead of the festive season, adding six stocks to its mid-cap portfolio and changing allocations in its large-cap portfolio. Here are key stocks that Kotak has identified after the market correction – Why Kotak sees opportunities after the market fall The brokerage identified three factors that could influence the market's next move - crude oil prices, corporate earnings and stock valuations. Uncertainty surrounding the Iran-US conflict and the risk of higher oil prices continue to weigh on India's economic outlook. However, earnings have offered some reassurance. According to the brokerage report, the Q2FY27 net profits for the Nifty 50 companies that had reported were 1.7% above its estimates and 19% higher year-on-year. Sanjeev Prasad, MD & Co-Head, Kotak Institutional Equities believes “that a greater focus on the favourable price-value gap in more stocks after the sharp correction in recent weeks will help dispel the ‘gloomy’ mood in the market.” In his strategy note, he pointed out that “many market participants are taking cues from prices and not from value, which has resulted in euphoria and despair in the market linked to price movements. We see value in more parts of the market , as valuations have come off sharply across sectors and stocks. Market multiples are reasonable, although we focus less on top-down index valuations.” ALSO READ7x earnings, a 59% fall: Vijay Kedia and Dolly Khanna’s latest smallcap bets Aster DM Healthcare: 37% upside potential Aster DM Healthcare is one of Kotak's new mid-cap portfolio additions. Its shares fell 15% in the past month amid concerns about possible government price controls on medicines and other hospital products. According to the brokerage report, the stock offers 37% potential upside to its 12-month fair value of Rs 880. Kotak believes its current valuation already reflects a moderate degree of government intervention. However, regulatory developments remain a risk. Dixon Technologies: 33% upside after the fall Dixon Technologies, which operates in electronics manufacturing services (EMS), is another stock returning to Kotak's recommended portfolio. Its shares declined 16% in the past month amid a broader market correction. The brokerage sees 33% potential upside to its 12-month fair value of Rs 14,900. It continues to favour the company's position in electronics manufacturing, although its valuation and business outlook need monitoring. Kotak on Emcure and Endurance Technologies Kotak sees 26% potential upside in Emcure Pharmaceuticals, with a fair value of Rs 2,225. The stock declined 9% in the past month amid concerns about possible drug price controls. The brokerage expects earnings per share (EPS) to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 17% between FY26-29. Endurance Technologies offers 34% potential upside to Kotak's fair value of Rs 3,000. Its shares fell 15% in the past month and 23% over the past year. The brokerage points to its exposure to two-wheeler exports and its progress in four-wheeler components. Indegene and Mankind Pharma: Healthcare in focus Indegene, which provides technology and outsourcing services to the global life sciences industry, offers 29% potential upside to Kotak's fair value of Rs 735. The brokerage expects the company to benefit from continued spending on digital transformation and outsourced services in the life sciences sector. Mankind Pharma has moved from Kotak's mid-cap portfolio to its large-cap portfolio, reflecting its market capitalisation of $9.6 billion. It is a portfolio reclassification, not a new addition to the overall recommended portfolio. ALSO READApplied for an IPO? Bajaj Finance replaces Bajaj Finserv, with both stocks retaining an unchanged portfolio weight of 480 basis points. The brokerage prefers Bajaj Finance as a more direct investment opportunity, even though Bajaj Finserv trades at a substantial discount to its sum-of-the-parts valuation. Reliance gains weight as Kotak trims other stocks Reliance Industries receives an increased allocation, with its portfolio weight rising by 100 basis points to 730 basis points. The brokerage has also trimmed HDFC Life Insurance by 25 basis points to 230 basis points, ICICI Bank by 50 basis points to 990 basis points, and Infosys by 75 basis points to 220 basis points. docs.title: Down 56.5%, trading at 23.5x earnings: An AI smallcap worth a fresh look
docs.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities for analytics companies. But a growing market does not automatically translate into higher profits. Companies still have to win clients, replace lost business and ensure that the money spent on new technology brings in enough revenue to justify the cost. Latent View Analytics is trying to do just that. The company helps businesses use data to make decisions and is investing in AI capabilities while deepening its relationship with Databricks, a data and AI platform. The opportunity is clear. Whether it can turn that opportunity into sustained growth without sacrificing margins is less certain. There are reasons to be optimistic. Latent View’s revenue grew 19.4% in US dollar terms in FY26, supported by growth in financial services and other non-technology businesses. Its Databricks-related business is also expanding, giving it another potential source of revenue as companies invest in data infrastructure and AI. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now Latent View Analytics 1-Year Share Price Chart Source: Screener.in A large technology client has reduced its business with Latent View, leaving the company with revenue to replace even as it continues to invest in AI, Databricks and senior talent. These investments may support future growth, but they also raise costs in the present. The company now has to demonstrate that new business can make up for what it has lost. Investors are becoming less willing to overlook these challenges. At Rs 225.30 on 26 October 2026, the stock was down around 56.5% from its 52-week high of Rs 517.50. The key question is whether Latent View can turn the AI opportunity into profitable growth. The challenge of replacing lost business For a services company, losing a large client is not just a question of replacing revenue. It also leaves the company with employees and costs that were supported by that business. Finding another client takes time, while salaries and other expenses continue to be paid. ALSO READ4 Smallcap Stocks to Watch for Long-Term Growth Navigating the Tech Vertical Slump Latent View saw this problem play out in its technology vertical, which declined 9.5% sequentially in the March 2026 quarter. Vendor consolidation, project rationalisation and a large client’s decision to bring some work in-house contributed to the fall. The company expects the lost business to have an annualised revenue impact of around US$6.5 million to US$7 million in FY27. Source: Company Presentation Management hopes to recover part of this through new AI-led deals and an improvement in technology spending. But new business does not arrive on a timetable that neatly matches the loss of old business. Until replacement revenue comes in, the company must contend with a gap between the costs it carries and the revenue it generates. There is some support elsewhere in the business. Latent View’s non-technology segments grew around 41% in FY26, helped by demand from areas such as financial services. The question is whether this growth can continue at a pace that offsets weakness in technology. Diversification helps, but it becomes a real cushion only when it can absorb a setback in one of the larger businesses. The Growth-Margin Paradox: Why More AI Means Less Profit The case for Latent View rests partly on a simple proposition: as companies adopt AI, they will need help making their data usable, connecting systems and building applications that deliver business results. This creates work for analytics companies even when the underlying AI models are developed by someone else. Latent View has been investing in these capabilities. Its FY26 commentary indicated that advanced AI accounted for about 49% of revenue when customer-facing AI implementations and AI embedded in workflows were combined. The company’s Q1 FY27 presentation reported AI-led revenue at around 35%, using a narrower definition. These figures are not directly comparable, but they suggest that AI-related work is already a meaningful part of the business. The more difficult question is what this growth costs. Latent View has been investing in specialised employees, senior leadership and newer technology platforms. In the March 2026 quarter, its adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 24.1%, partly because of higher visa expenses and spending on AI and Databricks. In the June quarter, the margin declined further to 20.4%. This is the tension in the AI opportunity. A company cannot afford to stand still while its clients change how they use technology. But investing ahead of demand means carrying costs before the revenue fully arrives. If new projects scale up, today’s spending could support tomorrow’s growth. If they do not, the company could end up with higher costs without a corresponding improvement in revenue. AI demand, by itself, is therefore not enough to establish the strength of the investment case. Investors also need to see whether that demand translates into profitable business. Databricks could become a bigger contributor Latent View’s relationship with Databricks gives it another way to participate in the growth of AI. Companies preparing their data infrastructure for AI applications may need help with data engineering, platform integration and analytics. A services provider with the right skills and client relationships can benefit from this spending. Latent View generated US$17.5 million in Databricks-related revenue in FY26, an increase of around 46% over the previous year. Management had indicated an ambition to grow this business by around 60% in FY27. If that happens, Databricks could make a larger contribution to the company’s overall growth. docs.title: Eicher to TVS Motor: Why Jefferies is betting on two-wheelers this festive season
docs.text: With the festive season in India in full swing, several interesting trends are popping up across sectors. One such trend is being seen in the auto sector. It is the big divergence in registrations for two-wheelers and passenger vehicles (PVs). Two-wheeler registrations are up 16% year-on-year (YoY) despite a high base, whereas PV registrations are down 6% YoY, global investment bank Jefferies said in a report, citing auto registration data. Jefferies prefers two-wheelers over four-wheelers among original equipment manufacturers. Strong demand momentum in two-wheelers The domestic two-wheeler industry is witnessing strong demand in the first half of the ongoing month-long festive season. Despite a high base post the goods and services tax cut in 2025, registrations have risen in the first 14 days of the festive season, from October 11 to October 24. ALSO READ4 Smallcap Stocks to Watch for Long-Term Growth For the first half of financial year 2027 (FY27), two-wheeler registrations grew 22% YoY while wholesales rose 17% YoY. PV demand tapering off Demand momentum in PVs seems to have moderated in the second week of the festive season, with registrations declining 6% YoY. PV registrations were healthy in the first week, rising 7% YoY. For the first half of FY27, PV registrations and wholesales grew 28-29% YoY. Truck, tractor registrations firm The festive season has started strong for trucks and tractors as well. “Truck registrations in the first 14 days are up 76% YoY, although boosted by low base as volumes declined 26% YoY in the corresponding period last year. Versus 2024, truck registrations have grown at 14% CAGR in the first half of the festive period,” Jefferies said. Tractor registrations are also up a healthy 21% YoY, although concerns remain on demand in the second half of FY27 due to a high base and a weak monsoon. Navratri sales Indians bought 11.23 lakh vehicles during the 10-day Navratri period this year, according to Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA). Vehicle retail sales rose nearly 27% compared with Navratri 2024, when Indian customers brought 8.86 lakh vehicles. However, vehicle retail sales declined 6.52% year-on-year compared to the 12.01 lakh units sold during Navratri 2025. “As we enter the Dhanteras-to-Diwali wave, we remain cautiously optimistic: affordability is strong, aspiration is rising, and auto retail continues to mirror the enduring momentum of the India Growth Story,” FADA President Sai Giridhar had said. However, FADA says, the comparison is not like-for-like as Navratri lasted 11 days last year, compared with 10 days this year. The festive period in 2025 also coincided with the rollout of GST 2.0, which brought forward pent-up demand. ALSO READAther to M&M, Hyundai: Nomura names 5 stocks to ride the EV shift in India Jefferies’ top auto picks Global investment bank Jefferies prefers two-wheelers over four-wheelers among original equipment manufacturers. Jefferies’ preferred ‘Buys’ are Eicher Motors and TVS Motor Company, followed by Mahindra & Mahindra. What investors should watch next? Demand for trucks, tractors, and two-wheelers remain firm while PV demand has been mixed. The festive demand and buying trends over the next two weeks remain key and will be monitored closely. docs.title: Aavas Financiers Q2 net profit rises 10.7%, but can low rains hurt the portfolio?
docs.text: Aavas Financiers reported stronger disbursements in the September quarter, supported by growth in its housing and non-housing loan businesses. However, pressure on lending spreads and a modest rise in overdue loans kept attention on the quality and profitability of its growth. Jefferies, Equirus Securities and InCred Capital remained positive on the company, although their views differed on the earnings outlook and valuation. Aavas Financiers Q2FY27 performance Aavas’ assets under management (AUM) rose 16.1% year on year to Rs 24,801 crore in Q2FY27. Disbursements increased 21.2% year on year to Rs 1,891 crore. The non-housing loan book grew 28.6%, compared with 10.1% growth in housing loans. Net interest income grew 12.7% year on year, while profit after tax rose 10.7%. Equirus noted that “Spread contraction drove an NII miss, while contained opex and lower provisions kept PPoP and PAT in line.” Gross stage 3 assets remained stable at 1.1%, while net stage 3 assets stood at 0.7%. Loans overdue by more than 30 days edged up to 3.81%. Jefferies maintains 'Buy' rating on Aavas Financiers Jefferies maintained its 'Buy' rating on Aavas Financiers. Jefferies’ assessment focused on asset quality and profitability. Gross stage 3 assets remained stable quarter on quarter, while overdue loans increased marginally. Pressure on lending margins remains important to the company’s earnings outlook. The report also discussed management’s expectation that the operating expense-to-assets ratio “should fall below 3% in the medium term.” Improving operating efficiency could support profitability as the loan book expands. ALSO READL&T to BEL, HAL: 12 defence stocks in focus after DAC clears Rs 2.12 lk cr procurement Equirus retains 'Long' rating on Aavas Financiers Equirus Securities retained its 'Long' rating and a September 2027 target price of Rs 1,795, implying 57.5% upside from the reference price. The brokerage forecast an 18% compound annual growth rate in AUM between FY26 and FY29, while trimming its margin estimates for FY27 and FY28. Equirus said there was “no impact of lower rains/drought on the portfolio quality and business momentum.” It also noted that management had retained its growth and credit-cost guidance. Aavas kept its FY27 AUM growth guidance at 16-17% and credit-cost guidance below 25 basis points. Equirus also noted that management expected spreads to remain above 5%, with employee productivity and operating cost control important to its longer-term plans. InCred Capital retains 'Add' rating but cuts target price InCred Capital retained its 'Add' rating but reduced its target price to Rs 1,550 from Rs 1,700, implying 36% upside from the reference price. The brokerage pointed to improving operating efficiency and loan growth, while noting that margins and asset quality remained key concerns. It wrote, “We appreciate the rising branch productivity to 1.25 files/month per officer vs 1.1 QoQ.” It also said, “Improving productivity and growth support outlook, although spread and asset quality remain key watchpoints.” InCred noted that disbursements rose 17% quarter on quarter and 21% year on year. It said Aavas had reiterated its guidance for around 20% year-on-year disbursement growth, with AUM growth of about 16-17% in FY27. Aavas Financiers outlook hinges on margins and productivity Aavas is expanding its loan book while keeping stage 3 asset ratios broadly stable, but margin pressure remains a key concern. Equirus expects sustained AUM growth, InCred sees scope for better productivity, and Jefferies’ view remains positive, although its latest target price could not be verified from the available report details. The company’s ability to convert stronger disbursements into sustained earnings growth will depend on managing funding costs, improving employee productivity and maintaining asset quality. docs.title: Apple iPad Mini OLED is a compact powerhouse at Rs 82,900, but is it for everyone?
docs.text: There’s a new iPad Mini in town and Apple has given it some serious upgrades. While the headline-worthy feature is said to be the new OLED display, Apple has added more to the mix. The new iPad Mini now features a 2-nanometer A20 Pro chip from the iPhone 18 Pro, an IP67 certification for water and dust resistance, and the celebrated 1,200-nit OLED display with reduced bezels. In a world where foldable smartphones are taking over compact tablets, the iPad Mini holds its ground as a high-spec compact tablet. The pricing of the new iPad Mini is still reasonable for anyone seeking a compact tablet. Starting at Rs 82,900 in India and going past Rs 1.36 lakh for top-tier cellular variants, the new iPad Mini sits firmly in premium territory. - The Wi-Fi lineup starts at Rs 82,900 for 128GB and goes up to Rs 94,900 for 256GB, and Rs 1,18,900 for 512GB. - Those opting for Wi-Fi plus 5G Cellular connectivity will look at Rs 1,00,900 for 128GB, Rs 1,12,900 for 256GB, and Rs 1,36,900 for the top 512GB tier. This price jump, paired with pro-tier features like optional nano-texture display glass and Wi-Fi 7, moves the small tablet away from casual e-reading and media consumption toward a niche set of power users. So, who actually needs an ultra-compact, professional-grade tablet? We figured out the target audience for this iPad. ALSO READMotorola Edge 70 Neo is trending on Google Trends and here’s why 1. Field professionals and on-site engineers With an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance, the new iPad Mini is designed to withstand harsh outdoor environments. Hence, for civil engineers on construction sites, aviation crews in tight cockpits, field researchers, and emergency medical personnel, the iPad Mini feels more in line rather than carrying a full-sized 11-inch or 13-inch iPad Pro. The 8.5-inch footprint allows comfortable one-handed operation while providing enough computational performance to render complex 3D CAD models, run real-time telemetry, or manage field documentation, all courtesy of the new A20 Pro chip. 2. Outdoor creators and digital illustrators For artists and creators, the iPad Mini’s display upgrades are designed to combat tricky environmental lighting. The 1,200-nit peak HDR brightness significantly improves outdoor legibility compared to older LCD panels, allowing creators to sketch in direct sunlight. On the 256GB and 512GB storage variants, Apple offers an optional nano-texture glass — a matte anti-glare finish that reduces reflections while adding subtle tactile friction when drawing with the Apple Pencil Pro. Combined with P3 wide colour support and the deep contrast ratios of the OLED technology, it becomes a digital sketchbook for on-the-go photo grading and illustration. 3. Executive travellers and digital nomads For frequent flyers and commuters, space inside a carry-on bag or small backpack comes at a premium. The iPad Mini OLED delivers full laptop-grade processing power via the A20 Pro chip and high-speed Wi-Fi 7 or 5G connectivity without taking up unnecessary room. Be it spreadsheets or 3D CAD renders, the iPad Mini has the power to deal with it easily. The repositioning of the 12MP ultra-wide front camera to the landscape edge addresses a long-standing complaint for video calls. Executive users can now join meetings and utilise Center Stage while resting the tablet naturally on an airplane tray table in landscape orientation. 4. Mobile gamers and on-set media operators The iPad Mini’s top-tier 512GB model features an additional CPU core alongside an upgraded GPU, turning the 8.5-inch tablet into a portable gaming device capable of handling hardware-accelerated ray tracing and demanding console-tier titles. For video production crews, the compact size and accurate colour representation make the tablet ideal as a high-brightness camera monitor or director's controller that clips easily onto gimbal rigs without throwing off calibration or adding weight. So, who should skip the iPad Mini? While the hardware upgrades are substantial, the iPad Mini OLED is not meant for every user. Budget-minded students and casual readers will find the price tag steep for simple web browsing, reading ebooks, or streaming video indoors. A standard 11-inch iPad or iPad Air offers a significantly larger screen area for multitasking at a much lower entry price. Similarly, desk-bound productivity seekers who rely on split-screen apps, multi-window desktop management, or typing long documents with a dedicated keyboard case are still far better served by an iPad Air, iPad Pro, or MacBook Air. The iPad Mini is simply too small for these requirements. ALSO READ Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra review: Ultimate productivity tablet or expensive compromise? Conclusion Apple’s new iPad Mini OLED is no longer just a shrunk-down tablet. Instead, it is a specialised tool for users who view portability as an absolute requirement rather than a compromise. It isn’t going to appeal to someone seeking a simple large screen experience for casual usage or addressing professional workflows, but a certain class fo consumers will appreciate the compact size and the sheer performance capability of the device.

docs.title: Jio Platforms: Motilal recommends long-term investment but Nomura prefers Bharti Airtel
docs.text: Jio Platforms’ Rs 30,213-crore initial public offering (IPO) closed for subscription on October 23, 2026, with the company fixing the issue price at Rs 1,119 per share and the listing on October 28, valuing the company at around Rs 10.3 lakh crore. Motilal Oswal Wealth Management sees long-term value citing Jio’s market leadership, earnings growth and opportunities in broadband, enterprise technology and AI. Nomura, meanwhile prefers Bharti Airtel, citing its premium subscriber mix and stronger ability to benefit from tariff increases. Jio Platforms IPO closes, listing scheduled for October 28 Jio Platforms’ IPO carried a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share and comprised an entirely fresh issue of shares, with no offer for sale. At the upper end of the price band, the issue implied a market capitalisation of around Rs 10.3 lakh crore. ALSO READMissed Jio IPO allotment? Analysts reveal entry levels for the telecom stock after listing The IPO proceeds were intended primarily for the prepayment or repayment of borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm, Jio Platforms’ material subsidiary, with the balance allocated to general corporate purposes. Motilal Oswal’s report listed up to Rs 27,500 crore for repayment or prepayment of borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm. The subscription window has closed, so Motilal Oswal’s recommendation to subscribe applied to investors considering the IPO during its offer period. Those who missed the issue will have to assess the stock after listing, at the prevailing market price. That price may be above or below the IPO price of Rs 1,119. Motilal Oswal recommends long-term investment Motilal Oswal Wealth Management’s report, titled Jio Platforms Limited, Subscribe for Listing Gains and Long Term, gave a positive view of the company’s market position, financial performance and growth opportunities. “Overall, we recommend investors to SUBSCRIBE for both listing gains and long term,” the brokerage said. The report added, “Jio offers a combination of market leadership, healthy earnings growth and future opportunities in broadband, enterprise technology and AI.” Motilal Oswal’s investment case rested on Jio’s scale in digital connectivity, improving monetisation and operating leverage. The brokerage described Jio as India’s largest digital connectivity platform by subscriber base, carrying around 60% of the country’s wireless data traffic. It also pointed to the company’s nationwide 5G network, built on proprietary technology, and its growing fixed wireless broadband business under JioAirFiber. Jio had 533 million subscribers and 14 million JioAirFiber customers, according to the report. Its digital services spanned cloud, enterprise solutions and artificial intelligence, while its patent portfolio and network technology offered additional avenues for growth. However, Motilal Oswal noted that connectivity remained the core earnings driver and that monetisation of newer digital services still needed to be demonstrated at scale. Jio revenue and profit growth betwee FY24-FY26 Motilal Oswal highlighted Jio’s consistent growth and profitability, with revenue and profit after tax growing at compound annual growth rates of around 16% and 18%, respectively, between FY24 and FY26. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,46,885.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,09,558.1 crore in FY24. Profit after tax increased to Rs 30,049.1 crore from Rs 21,423.2 crore over the same period. EBITDA rose to Rs 76,255.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 54,958.7 crore in FY24. EBITDA margin widened to 51.91% in FY26 from 50.16% in FY24, reaching 53.26% in the June 2026 quarter. In Q1FY27, Jio reported revenue from operations of Rs 39,172.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 20,864.5 crore and profit after tax of Rs 7,764.1 crore. The brokerage noted that revenue and EBITDA grew around 11.8% and 15%, respectively, year on year in the June quarter. Motilal Oswal also pointed to cash generation as 5G capital expenditure moderated. EBITDA less cash capital expenditure increased to Rs 42,071.1 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,449.1 crore in FY24, according to the report. Jio Platform ARPU, tariff hike, broadband key monitorables Motilal Oswal identified improving monetisation as another strength. Jio’s average revenue per user (ARPU) increased from Rs 181.7 in FY24 to Rs 214 in FY26 and Rs 215.6 in the June 2026 quarter. Data consumption also increased, reaching 42.3 GB per customer per month in FY26, compared with 28.7 GB in FY24. The report recorded monthly churn of 1.61% in Q1FY27. The brokerage said higher data consumption, tariff hikes and fixed broadband expansion offered scope for further growth. Jio’s proprietary 5G technology, JioAirFiber business and enterprise and cloud offerings provided additional opportunities, although their contribution to earnings would need to grow over time. The report also identified risks. Connectivity remained the main earnings driver, and monetisation of newer digital services and AI offerings had yet to be demonstrated at scale. Motilal Oswal listed capital intensity, tariff and competition risks, spectrum and licensing requirements, promoter control, and technology and security as areas to monitor. At the upper end of the IPO price band, Motilal Oswal valued Jio at around 34 times post-issue FY26 earnings, compared with Bharti Airtel's trailing price-to-earnings multiple of around 40.7 times. It also noted Jio’s net leverage of 0.36 times. However, return on capital employed of around 10.8% and ARPU below Airtel’s were identified as key monitorables. docs.title: Brazil Stock Market Crash Explained: Why Lula’s election win triggered a 13.88% plunge
docs.text: Political events, especially unexpected election outcomes, significantly affect a country’s stock market. They shake investor confidence and cause sharp market movements. This was seen in Brazil’s election this week. Brazilian stocks and the real currency suffered heavy losses after the unexpected reelection of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. How Bad Was the Fall? The IBOVESPA, Brazil’s major stock market index, tracks around 50 of the most liquid stocks. It plunged 13.88% to close at 176,608, its biggest daily drop since March 2020. At one point, the index was down by 30% before a recovery happened. One of the biggest ETFs tracking the index, iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ), closed 19% down as all major index heavyweights plunged sharply. The real fell over 11% against the US dollar in early trading, marking one of its largest intraday declines. What Triggered the Crash? What led to this dramatic fall? The Brazil stock market crash of October 2026 came on account of President Lula’s victory over Flávio Bolsonaro in the presidential runoff, even after losing the first-round. Lula, a prominent member of the Workers’ Party, secured victory in the second-round vote against right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who was viewed as a more business-friendly candidate. This marks Lula’s third term as president. ALSO READ50 Nasdaq-100 stocks are either in the red or up less than 10% as index hits record high Why Did the Market Swing So Wildly? The results reversed the market reaction seen earlier. Flavio defeated Lula in the first round on October 4, marking Lula’s first defeat since 1998. After that, Brazil’s stock market surged by over 8%, and the real rallied by 4% against the dollar on the same day. The latest decline wiped out those gains. Investors viewed a Bolsonaro administration as more likely to curb public spending. That was seen as key to lowering interest rates. Markets are now reassessing fiscal risks, including persistent primary deficits and rising public debt, alongside institutional uncertainty around the election. Brazil stock market crash after election IndicatorPerformanceIBOVESPA fall13.88%Intraday decline30.00%iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ)-19.00%Brazilian real against US dollarDown over 11% intradayOctober 4, 2026, first roundIBOVESPA surged over 8% ; Real rallied 4% against the dollarOctober 2026, runoff resultIBOVESPA plunged 13.88% ; Real fell over 11% intraday Source: Yahoo Finance Is Brazil’s Debt Pile a Worry? Brazil’s public debt has surged more than 10 percentage points during Lula’s current term to over 82% of GDP, driving up borrowing costs. The root cause of the fiscal challenges is rising mandatory spending, which limits the adjustable federal budget to under 8%. Lula has shown mixed responses to debt issues, sometimes downplaying them while claiming that economic growth will resolve the situation. His team has committed to maintaining current budget rules that limit spending growth and set primary balance targets. This comes despite promises to increase the minimum wage and enhance welfare benefits. Inflation Is Running Above Target Brazil’s annual inflation stands at 4.6%, exceeding the central bank’s tolerance range of 1.5% to 4.5%, despite interest rates of 13.75%. The central bank has made five consecutive rate cuts amid signs of economic slowdown. Inflation is anticipated to remain above the 3% target until at least 2029. Elections and Markets Not just Brazil, many other major global economies have faced severe stock market shocks from unexpected election results. Indices can swing violently within a single trading day when outcomes differ from market expectations. India, June 2024: When Exit Polls Got It Wrong Closer home, a similar event happened during India’s June 2024 General Election. The Nifty 50 dropped sharply in one day, wiping out several lakh crores in investor wealth. Exit polls had indicated a significant victory for the ruling BJP. The actual results showed the party lost its standalone majority, and that led to panic-selling among investors. Mexico and Argentina Saw It Too In the same month of 2024, Mexico saw a similar impact. The Mexican Stock Exchange’s benchmark index declined over 6% after the election results were announced. It was the worst single-day drop since the early COVID-19 pandemic. Earlier, in 2019, the Argentine stock market dropped 35%, and the peso lost 25% of its value against the US dollar. This followed unexpected primary election results, where President Mauricio Macri underperformed significantly. Can an Election Result Also Spark a Rally? The reverse is also true. When political uncertainty clears or a highly pro-business government wins a decisive mandate, global stock markets can see explosive, historic rallies. 18 May 2009 remains one such day for Indian stock market investors. The United Progressive Alliance (UPA) secured a strong majority in 2009, and that led to significant market enthusiasm. The Nifty 50 hit its 20% “upper circuit limit,” and the National Stock Exchange of India suspended trading shortly after opening. Should Long-Term Investors Worry? An election-day rally or crash is generally a one-day event, and markets take a more balanced view over time. For long-term investors, such events need no panic reaction. Political parties drive a nation’s economic policies, and the mandate they receive on results day paves the path for future reforms. History shows that no such one-day event has shaped the outcome for equity markets over the long term. Readers should consult a qualified financial adviser before making investment decisions.

docs.title: Already up 65% YTD! Motilal Oswal sees a further 36% upside in this power stock - Check target price
docs.text:
Already up 65% YTD! Motilal Oswal sees a further 36% upside in this power stock - Check target price
 UTLSOLAR 
 New Delhi, Oct. 27 -- A power stock has been on a bull run this year so far, yet brokerage firm Motilal Oswal Financial Services sees further upside in this stock and recommends buying the stock now. 
 Shares of Fujiyama Power Systems, a rooftop solar solutions provider company, ended 1.38% higher at Rs.368.40 on the BSE on Tuesday, 27 October, extending gains for the second consecutive session. 
 Fujiyama Power Systems shares are up 65% year-to-date (YTD) compared to a 14% fall in the equity benchmark Sensex. 
 Over the last six months, the stock has gained 21.50% compared to a 5% fall in the Sensex. 
 On 20 August this year, the stock rose to its 52-week high of Rs.494 after hitting a 52-week low of Rs.170.55 on 2 March. 
 In a report dated 26 October, Motilal Oswal Financial Services recommended a 'buy' rating on the stock with a target price of Rs.500. This implies an upside potential of 36% from the stock's 27 October closing of Rs.368.40 on the BSE. 
 Motilal Oswal expects the company to clock a CAGR of 52%, 57%, and 59% in revenue, EBITDA, and adjusted PAT, respectively, during FY26-28. 
 Motilal Oswal underscored that China has proposed export restrictions on 16th October on advanced solar manufacturing technologies, including tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon), heterojunction technology (HJT) and x-back contact (XBC), as well as thin-wafer,perovskite and tandem technologies. The curbs are not expected to impact Fujiyama Power Systems, as it has already secured a technology transfer agreement from China. 
 According to the brokerage firm, this supports the development of its 1.2GW TOPCon cell manufacturing facility at Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh. Commercial production at this facility is expected to commence in the first half of FY28. 
 China dominates solar cell manufacturing. It also accounts for nearly 97% of global wafer manufacturing capacity. Motilal believes that, given surplus capacity and the importance of overseas markets, outright export restrictions on cells and wafers may be less likely. 
 "India's shift toward integrated solar-plus-storage solutions and proposed domestic content requirements for inverters and batteries under the next phase of the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana could benefit Fujiyama Power," said Motilal. 
 "The company has installed a 5MW battery energy storage system (BESS) at Dadri and plans an additional 10MW system at Ratlam, supporting its entry into the commercial and industrial storage market by leveraging its existing rooftop solar portfolio and distribution network," Motilal Oswal said.

Diwali 2026 Muhurat picks: Brokerage firm Axis Securities, in its latest report titled as ‘Axis Diwali Mahurat Picks: SAMVAT 2083’, has listed out top nine stocks to buy for long-term with an upside potential up to 20%.
Meanwhile, benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty opened lower on Tuesday, weighed down by persistently high crude oil prices and selling pressure in IT stocks. The 30-share BSE Sensex fell 281.95 points to 73,316.21 in early trading, while the 50-share NSE Nifty dropped 63.15 points to 22,694.60.Diwali 2026: Stock market outlookBrokerage firm Axis Securities said that returns over Diwali 2026 to Diwali 2027 will increasingly depend on buying the right businesses at sensible valuations, monitoring earnings delivery and avoiding excessive concentration in expensive or speculative ideas.It further added that the coming Samvat is likely to be shaped by the interaction of global inflation, crude oil prices, monetary-policy decisions, foreign capital flows and domestic earnings delivery. docs.text:
Against this backdrop, Nuvama Institutional Equities has initiated coverage on Milky Mist Dairy Food with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of ₹ 330, citing the company’s strong growth outlook, premium value-added dairy portfolio and improving cash flows as it transitions from a phase of heavy capital expenditure to a period of stronger returns. Nuvama believes the stock could continue to command a premium valuation, supported by its growth profile and focus on value-added dairy products (VADP). The brokerage has valued the company at 50 times its estimated September 2028 earnings per share (EPS), a premium to peers. The brokerage expects Milky Mist to deliver a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 27% in revenue, 35% in EBITDA and 57% in earnings per share over FY26–FY29. Growth is expected to be driven by its core categories of paneer, cheese and curd, expansion in yoghurt and ice cream, and a wider geographical presence beyond South India. However, Nuvama flagged risks arising from milk price volatility and the company’s geographical and manufacturing concentration. Around 95% of its milk procurement comes from Tamil Nadu, while approximately 69% of sales are generated in South India. The company also relies on a single plant, making operational concentration a key risk. Nuvama described Milky Mist as India’s only pure-play value-added dairy company and a high-growth consumer business. The company’s revenue grew at a CAGR of 31% between FY24 and FY26, while EBITDA expanded at a 41% CAGR. In the first quarter of FY27, revenue increased 43.6% year-on-year, accompanied by a 275-basis-point improvement in gross margin. Milky Mist has a portfolio spanning more than 20 categories, entirely focused on value-added dairy products, with no liquid milk business. According to Nuvama, the company is the largest private packaged brand in paneer, with around 19% of the organised market, and holds approximately 12% of the South Indian cheese market. It is also among the top two private packaged yoghurt brands, with a market share of about 13%. The brokerage sees further growth opportunities in protein-rich categories such as curd, paneer, cheese and whey, where demand is supported by increasing consumer interest in higher-protein foods. Nuvama estimates that paneer, cheese and curd account for approximately 60% of Milky Mist’s revenue and expects these categories to grow at a combined CAGR of around 28% over FY26–FY29. Paneer, which contributes approximately 30% of revenue, is expected to grow at a CAGR of 29%. The brokerage believes the shift towards organised players, supported by restrictions on analogue paneer and zero GST, could benefit the company. Cheese revenue is projected to grow at a CAGR of 29%, aided by capacity expansion in cheddar, while curd is expected to record a 24% CAGR over the same period. Nuvama expects yoghurt and ice cream to grow at CAGRs of 45% and 35%, respectively, over FY26–FY29. Their combined contribution to revenue is projected to increase from 13% to 17%. The brokerage highlighted Greek yoghurt and Skyr as key products in Milky Mist’s premium, high-protein portfolio. Capacity expansion in yoghurt is expected to support the company’s plans to scale these categories. 50,000-plus coolers and freezers to support expansion beyond South India Milky Mist plans to deploy more than 50,000 coolers and freezers over the next three years, compared with an existing base of approximately 41,000. Nuvama believes this investment will help improve product availability and strengthen distribution in markets beyond South India. The brokerage expects revenue from non-South markets to grow at a CAGR of 32% over FY26–FY29 as the company expands its distribution network. Nuvama expects Milky Mist’s EBITDA margin to increase to 16.5% by FY29 from 13.7% in FY26, an improvement of 280 basis points. Gross margin is projected to rise to 35.2% from 33% over the same period. The brokerage estimates that the company’s existing manufacturing capacity can support revenue of 3–3.5 times its FY26 level, providing room for growth without a proportionate increase in capital expenditure. Nuvama expects Milky Mist’s gross debt to decline by more than half, from ₹ 1,670 crore in FY26 to ₹ 720 crore by FY29, supported by IPO proceeds and stronger cash generation. The company is expected to retain approximately ₹ 700 crore in lower-cost borrowings that benefit from a government interest subsidy of around 3%. The brokerage also expects return on capital employed (RoCE) to improve to 20.4% from 13.4%. Free cash flow is projected to reach approximately 64% of profit after tax by FY29, compared with negative free cash flow in FY26. Nuvama’s positive outlook rests on Milky Mist’s ability to sustain strong growth in value-added dairy products, expand its presence beyond the South and improve profitability as its capital expenditure cycle moderates. However, milk price fluctuations and the concentration of procurement, manufacturing and sales remain key risks to monitor. Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only. Here's why Kotak Neo recommends 'Buy' rating on ICICI Bank; 'Add' Nykaa
 Nykaa offers an attractive combination of category leadership, strong execution, multiple growth levers, and improving profitability, says Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research at Kotak Neo.
 Kotak Neo has a 'Buy' rating on ICICI Bank, and maintains 'Add' rating on Nykaa.
 Shrikant Chouhan Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 27 2026 | 7:56 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research, Kotak Neo. FSN E-commerce Ventures (NYKAA): ADD CMP: ₹330 FV: ₹370 Resistance: ₹335/345 Support: ₹320/313 FSN E-commerce Ventures (NYKAA) is India's leading omnichannel beauty, personal care, and fashion retailer, supported by a strong consumer franchise, differentiated omnichannel presence, and a growing portfolio of owned brands. The company is well-positioned to capitalize on structural tailwinds from rising discretionary consumption, increasing online penetration, premiumization, and growing demand for beauty and personal care products. Strong Q2FY27 business momentum: Nykaa reported a robust Q2FY27 business update, with broad-based growth across both Beauty & Personal Care (BPC) and Fashion segments. The update highlights resilient consumer demand and reinforces the company's healthy growth trajectory ahead of the festive season. Continued market share gains, strong customer engagement, and expansion across categories remain key growth drivers. Compelling growth outlook: We expect Nykaa to deliver a healthy ~27 per cent revenue CAGR over FY26-29E, led by sustained momentum in the BPC business, rapid Fashion scale-up, category expansion, premiumization trends, and increasing contribution from owned brands. The BPC segment, Nykaa's core business, is expected to maintain its leadership position and deliver ~27 per cent revenue CAGR during FY26-29E, supported by strong brand partnerships and favorable industry dynamics. Earnings growth to outpace revenue growth: Beyond strong top-line expansion, Nykaa is entering a phase of improving profitability. Higher operating leverage, better fulfillment efficiencies, moderation in customer acquisition costs, and a growing mix of owned brands are expected to drive margin expansion. Consequently, we estimate a ~90 per cent PAT CAGR over FY26-29E, significantly outpacing revenue growth and underscoring the scalability of the business model. We believe Nykaa offers an attractive combination of category leadership, strong execution, multiple growth levers, and improving profitability. With Beauty continuing to compound strongly and Fashion gradually scaling up, the company remains well-positioned to create long-term shareholder value. We remain positive on the stock and maintain our ADD rating, with a revised DCF-based fair value of ₹370 per share. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE ICICI Bank: BUY CMP: ₹1,403 FV: ₹1,800 Resistance: ₹1,415/1435 Support: ₹1,380/1365 ICICI Bank is one of India’s leading private sector banks, offering a diversified suite of banking and financial services across retail, rural, business banking and corporate lending, alongside subsidiaries in life insurance, general insurance, securities and other financial services. Its loan book is predominantly domestic, with a growing international portfolio. Strong and diversified loan growth: As of Q2FY27, advances stood at ₹18.3 lakh crore, growing 30 per cent YoY, or approximately 24 per cent excluding loans against FCNR(B) deposits. The domestic book grew 23 per cent, led by business banking (+34 per cent), corporate loans (+31 per cent) and retail and rural loans (+15 per cent). Within retail, mortgages grew 15 per cent and personal loans 17 per cent. The bank’s diversified loan mix, with a declining share of corporate loans over the past decade, supports balanced growth. Superior execution and earnings momentum: Q2FY27 net profit grew 20 per cent YoY, supported by 18 per cent growth in net interest income (NII), approximately 19 per cent growth in pre-provision operating profit and a 7 per cent decline in provisions. Fee income grew 20 per cent YoY, reflecting healthy non-interest income momentum. Operating expenses rose just 8 per cent, demonstrating cost discipline and operating leverage. Strong asset quality and underwriting discipline: Gross and net NPA ratios stood at 1.2 per cent and 0.3 per cent, respectively, while credit costs remained low at 0.2 per cent of advances. Gross slippages declined to 1.2 per cent, with negligible new NPA formation in the corporate portfolio. The bank has sustained growth without aggressive lending in riskier segments, supported by disciplined underwriting and a provision buffer of ₹238 billion. The valuation incorporates around 2.5x book value, while subsidiaries contribute meaningful additional value. ICICI Bank’s consistent execution and superior profitability justify a premium to peers. Overall, strong growth, disciplined risk management, cost efficiency and potential margin recovery underpin the investment thesis.
